TCU firing Sonny Dykes this week is a new development, but Texas Tech's statistical edge and the Horned Frogs' absence of starting quarterback Jaden Craig were already factored into the opening line . The Horned Frogs also have the third-best red-zone defense nationally, which could compound Texas Tech's struggles in high-leverage situations and force the Red Raiders to settle for field goals. Meanwhile, both offensive lines struggle with pass protection and both defenses have high sack rates, opening the door for drive-killing sacks. If TCU can avoid giving the Red Raiders short fields, Texas Tech might have to chew up a significant amount of clock to build a comfortable lead. Furthermore, a two-score deficit wouldn't necessarily force the Horned Frogs to abandon their offensive game plan early, especially if their defense is keeping them within striking distance. Defensive coordinator Andy Avalos will take over as interim head coach as TCU looks to navigate the coaching change and secure bowl eligibility. Texas Tech has been productive offensively, averaging 444.4 yards of total offense per game. The Red Raiders are looking to earn a spot in the Big 12 Championship game and make the College Football Playoff . Tech will need to be disciplined and lean on starting quarterback Thomas Castellanos , who has thrown for 985 yards, 14 touchdowns and three interceptions this season. While the Frogs will look to rally behind Avalos and fight for bowl eligibility, the uncertainly following Dykes' departure and Craig's status at quarterback will make it too difficult to overcome Texas Tech's momentum and home-field advantage. Score prediction Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The regular season comes to an end in Galaxy Stadium for the Texas Tech football team , with TCU coming to town for a Thanksgiving showdown under the lights. There's a lot going on here, but we'll begin with TCU, which will have a new coach running things and a new quarterback running the show. Well, not entirely new. Adam Schobel took the reins against Utah after starter Jaden Craig missed the game due to injury. TCU has already ruled Craig out for this week's game, so Schobel will take snaps and try to lead the upset over Texas Tech. The 6-foot-5 sophomore had one pass attempt this season before going 15-of-31 for 106 yards and throwing two interceptions against the Utes. But this game is less about matchups and more about what's on the line. What's at stake for Texas Tech football Things are pretty simple for the Red Raiders this week. Beat the Horned Frogs and they're heading back to AT&T Stadium on Dec. 4 for the Big 12 Conference championship game against Utah, which has already clinched a spot in the title encounter. A loss to TCU does two things. First, it makes Texas Tech wait another two days to figure out if it's heading to Arlington, needing BYU to lose to Cincinnati. Second, no win over TCU and no BYU loss means Tech can pretty much kiss its College Football Playoff chances goodbye. Speaking of the CFP, this could be an important factor in Tech's inclusion this year. Texas Tech currently has the one-loss appeal that could get them into the field as an at-large bid, likely on the road to start the bracket. Losing the game would wipe that possibility out entirely. Something to consider is that Texas Tech just getting to the Big 12 title game probably wouldn't keep them safe in the CFP field regardless of the outcome in Arlington. With the 12-team CFP field expiring this year, the committee doesn't have much reason to protect the participants of conference championship games, which are fading away after this season to make way for the 24-team playoff next year. Texas Tech's J'Koby Williams runs with the ball against Arizona State during a Big 12 Conference football game, Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026, at Galaxy Stadium. The fired coach theory and TCU TCU made the move to part ways with Sonny Dykes following the team's 38-17 loss to Utah. Things haven't worked out well in Fort Worth since Dykes took the Horned Frogs to the national championship game. Despite two nine-win seasons since then, TCU has lacked consistency in a Big 12 that's been gettable with some form of success the last few years. The question for TCU becomes: will it follow the trend of firing your coach and coming out the next game with your hair on fire? TCU is the fifth power-conference team to have parted with its head coach during the 2026 season, the others being Baylor, NC State, Maryland, and Florida State. Of those four other teams switching coaches in season, three of them won their next game, two of them (Baylor and NC State) earning wins of 21 points or more. This theory doesn't always come to fruition, however. During the 2025 coaching cycle, six power-conference programs fired coaches during the season and just one of them won their next game following the axing. That one win came from Virginia Tech, which beat Wofford, so it barely counts. Score prediction for Texas Tech football vs TCU Texas Tech 34, TCU 31: TCU's staff and players are all trying to impress whoever the next head coach is, so they'll be pulling out all the stops in this one. Texas Tech has to manage that, but the home crowd gets them back to Arlington. The question for TCU becomes: will it follow the trend of firing your coach and coming out the next game with your hair on fire? TCU is the fifth power-conference team to have parted with its head coach during the 2026 season, the others being Baylor, NC State, Maryland, and Florida State. Texas Tech 34, TCU 31: TCU's staff and players are all trying to impress whoever the next head coach is, so they'll be pulling out all the stops in this one. Texas Tech has to manage that, but the home crowd gets them back to Arlington. There's a lot going on here, but we'll begin with TCU, which will have a new coach running things and a new quarterback running the show. But this game is less about matchups and more about what's on the line. What's at stake for Texas Tech football Things are pretty simple for the Red Raiders this week. Beat the Horned Frogs and they're heading back to AT&T Stadium on Dec. 4 for the Big 12 Conference championship game against Utah, which has already clinched a spot in the title encounter. Something to consider is that Texas Tech just getting to the Big 12 title game probably wouldn't keep them safe in the CFP field regardless of the outcome in Arlington. With the 12-team CFP field expiring this year, the committee doesn't have much reason to protect the participants of conference championship games, which are fading away after this season to make way for the 24-team playoff next year. picks.blurb: Florida Gators at Florida State Preview: How Do Gators Match Up vs. Seminoles? Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM GATORS FB SI.COM GATORS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS For the third time ever, the Florida Gators will face the Florida State Seminoles on Black Friday at Doak Campbell Stadium. Florida State has had a very underwhelming season, sitting at 5-6 after firing head coach Mike Norvell a few weeks ago and just announcing they'll hire Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schuman as the next head coach. This will be the 70th all-time matchup between these two in-state rivals, with Florida leading the series 39-28-2 all time. The Gators are looking for their third straight victory in the rivalry. Florida has the opportunity in this one to not only win eight regular-season games for the first time since 2020, but also keep their counterparts from making a bowl game. It may not have been a pretty last couple of weeks for the Gators, but a chance to finish the season winning three straight, building momentum for the future, is a good starting point for year one under a new head coach. On the other hand, the Seminoles are coming off arguably their worst loss of the season at home, losing by 18 points to a 5-6 NC State team. Although, the Seminoles are 2-1 since firing head coach Mike Norvell, with Rock Stockstill at the helm. A look at Florida State The Seminoles have dealt with a lot of injuries to key players like wide receiver Duce Robinson, running back Ousman Kromah, and multiple defensive players, including team sack leader Rylan Kennedy, plus inconsistent play this season. Offensively, the Seminoles are headlined by Auburn transfer quarterback Ashton Daniels. Daniels is a volatile quarterback accounting for 27 total touchdowns this year (14 passing, 13 rushing) and 14 interceptions. Daniels is a good athlete who can make explosive plays through the air and with his legs but is prone to costly mistakes. “Yeah, I think the quarterback's talented,” Jon Sumrall said. “He's athletic. He's played a lot of college football. He's a playmaker. He can extend plays, great plays with his legs. He can make all the throws. Their receiving core to me, is really scary. “I think this No. 8, 7, 15, all three of those guys I think are big-time players. The 8 guy, No. 8, Danzy's got elite top-end speed. I think 7, he's got a basketball background. He's a very natural, efficient mover. And then 15's got really good ball skills. I know they've been banged up a little bit at running back. That's been a challenge for them.” Pick your champion (you can change it later). We’ll email you when brackets open. No purchase necessary. 50 U.S./D.C. 18+. The College Football Playoff (CFP) is not a sponsor or administrator of this contest. As Sumrall said, their top playmakers are receievrs Micahi Danzy, Jayvan Boggs and Jansen Lopez. Last week against NC State, the Noles were missing their top four running backs, so expect a more pass-heavy attack from FSU. The 'Noles rank around league average in the ACC in points per game with 27.5 and total yards per game at 385.3. Defensively, Florida State is towards the bottom third of the league in total yards per game at 407.7 and points per game at 26.6. The Seminoles' rush defense also ranks in the bottom three in the conference. The Seminole defense is led by linebacker Chris Jones, who leads the team in all tackle categories, and defensive back Ashland Barker who is a long, lengthy corner who is tied for the team lead in interceptions. The Gators offensively need to get the ground game working for numerous reasons. Jadan Baugh is 20 yards short of 1,000 rushing yards ; Florida State's run defense is arguably their worst unit on their team, and in the Gators four losses this season Baugh has averaged a mere 36.3 rushing yards per game. Defensively, the Gators have to contain quarterback Ashton Daniels and force him into tough throwing windows while also limiting his escapability, which he loves to do to extend drives and create explosive plays. Sumrall highlights how important it is to win in-state rivalry games while also how it helps with winning in-state recruiting battles. "You want to win the state,” Sumrall said. “That's a big deal. I have a lot of respect for everybody we play in-state, or even the ones we don't. But you want to win the in-state battles, whether it be on the field or in recruiting, whatever. We compete every day, and so it's a huge deal. “Coach Meyer texted me maybe around the Texas game, and just said, 'Hey, finish this thing strong all the way down the stretch in November. Recruit the roster you need to recruit to build this thing.' And so he emphasized the reason to finish in November in a lot of ways, and getting some momentum as you go into the offseason as you build for the future, and this game is a big part of it. “And in-state rivalries, they matter. Anybody that says just another game, I don't buy into that. It's not just another game; it's an in-state rivalry. Those are different, but the world we live in are all big because we play in the SEC, and week in, week out, they're all big games, and they're all challenging games. This is one that means something to so many people "Because the in-state rivalry component, it is a bragging-rights in-state game, which does matter." The Gators cannot afford to overlook a disappointing Florida State squad as kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. EST this afternoon on ABC. Here's my Florida vs. Florida State prediction and college football pick for Friday, November 27, 2026. Florida vs. Florida State Pick: Florida -6 (-112) My Florida St vs. Florida best bet is on the Gators against the spread. Florida vs Florida State Odds Florida vs Florida State point spread : Florida -6.5 (-110), Florida St +6.5 (-110) Florida vs Florida State over/under : 53.5 (-110o / -110u) Florida vs Florida State moneyline : Florida -230, Florida St +190 Florida started off the Jon Sumrall era scorching hot. Its offense seemed impossible to stop, hanging 52 on Ole Miss in Week 4. But inconsistency has been rampant across the team, with all four of Florida's losses coming by 16-plus points. Outside of that Ole Miss trouncing — a game that came off the back of a wildly emotional Rebels win over LSU — Florida has a negative point margin in SEC play. There are two big wins over Texas and Kentucky (both on the road) but also a one-score sweat over Vanderbilt at home. Florida is a mystery box each and every week. Florida's offensive line has been a root of the issue in an offense that's very much run-first. Early downs have become predictable, with the featured player being Jadan Baugh (960 yards, SEC-leading 16 rushing touchdowns). Quarterback Aaron Philo has been utilized well when healthy, rushing for almost 200 yards and three touchdowns over the past two games, and Florida converts regularly on late downs. Two major issues plague Florida's defense, and they've blown the floodgates open: it allows too many consistent chunk plays through the air and cannot get off the field on late downs. The Gators rank 125th nationally in third/fourth-down success rate (50.3%) and 121st in Passing Success Rate. Jayden Woods and Emmanuel Oyebadejo make up one of the SEC's most productive pass-rush duos, with 14 combined sacks (Oyebadejo notched two of his own last week). But when the rush isn't getting home, Florida's secondary struggles to contain production. The best of Florida gives you one of the best football teams in the country. But there's been more bad than good lately, and Florida's floor is the bottom third of the SEC. Florida State 's long nightmare is over as Mike Norvell finally got the axe. Not only that, but FSU already has its next head coach lined up: Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann. But until Schumann takes over, Rick Stockstill will lead the 'Noles as interim head coach. Under Stockstill, FSU is 2-1, with one-score wins over a free-falling Pitt (lost five of its last six) and Boston College, along with a 28-10 loss to NC State last week. Not super inspiring results, to say the least. Against NC State, Florida State gained just 36% of available yards and hit the Red Zone just once (on the opening drive). It put the ball in harm's way four times, fortunately recovering both fumbles but also throwing two interceptions. Quarterback Ashton Daniels is now up to 14 picks thrown on the year, the most among FBS arms. The run game has struggled without Ousmane Kromah (out for the year with an ankle injury), and the throw game has struggled without Duce Robinson (torn ACL). Four-star freshman Amari Thomas left early last week, and Tre Wisner hasn't played since Week 10. This is an offense limping to the finish line, with a quarterback doing everything he can as his eligibility runs out. The Seminoles don't have the horses to be effective in the Gus Malzahn-esque option system. Offensive struggle usually comes with a defensive slip (see: Ohio State ). FSU hasn't played a quality offense since Miami (43 points allowed in a pair of overtimes) and Louisville (44 allowed the week before). Since then, it's been a run of injured teams that didn't have much offensive prowess to begin with. Of course, FSU is capable of getting up for one more game against bitter rival Florida. These intrastate rivalries in the Sunshine State are packed with genuine vitriol, and this roster will do everything but roll over and die, especially since a good chunk of it is still Florida-grown. Florida is a six-point road favorite this Saturday, with an over/under of 53.5. Florida has been bad as a favorite this year, posting a 2-6 ATS record with three outright losses. Meanwhile, Florida State is 4-1-1 ATS as an underdog this season. This line remained unchanged since the lookahead line posted this summer for both the total and spread. Florida State's roster has been decimated. Its top weapons are out for the remainder of the season, and the two fill-ins in the backfield are both banged up. For a run-first team, losing that kind of firepower in the backfield is a massive handicap. With the Schumann era on the doorstep and with a roster missing significant portions of its lineup, this is a game Florida State might just be happy to get over with, even if it is against an in-state rival. Favorites have covered each of the last four in this series, with Florida running away with the last two meetings. The Gators are much healthier coming into this matchup with more stability in the coaching ranks heading into 2027. This is a numbers play. Anything at +7 or better is probably a bet on FSU, while anything under is all Florida. Pick: Florida -6 (-112, DraftKings | Play to -6.5)

Florida is 20th in the latest College Football Playoff rankings after winning two straight to turn the season back around after a rough stretch. Florida State is waiting for new head coach Glenn Schumann to start, but the Georgia defensive coordinator is still a little busy for a bit at his current gig. The passing game is dangerous, but the Noles don't win when they bomb away. They win when they get things going on the ground, going 4-1 when running for 175 yards or more. It's possible to run on the Gators, but Florida State isn't Georgia, or even Missouri, when it comes to being able to grind. And then there's the other side. Florida is 7-0 when running for more than 120 yards. Run well on the Noles, beat the Noles. Why Florida State Will Win Everyone wants to win a rivalry game like this, and of course Florida will bring the full focus, but this is existential for the Seminoles. It'll be iffy whether or not the program would want to accept a bowl invite, or be able to, considering the regime change, but this is for six wins. This is for a bowl game. Florida's defense isn't bad, but it doesn't come up with enough third down stops. Florida State has to control the positive momentum from the start. It doesn't need big plays, but with its tempo, it has to keep the Gators on their heels with a good offensive balance. Florida vs Florida State Prediction, Betting Lines This should be fun. There's a new energy around the Florida State program, the team will come up with a strong first quarter, and then the Gator offense will start to take over. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. and will be televised on ABC. Florida State (5-6, 3-5 ACC) and Florida (7-4, 5-4 SEC) will meet for the 70th time, with Florida leading the all-time series 39-28-2, and winners of the last two matchups (40-21 in 2025 and 31-11 in 2024). FSU is 2-0 against the Gators on Fridays, winning 27-16 in 1979 and 45-38 in 2022, and the Noles have beaten five ranked SEC teams in the regular season since 2015, the most nationally among non-SEC programs. The Seminoles have started four running backs this season, including junior Zay Parks last week against NC State. Parks began his career as a walk-on and combined for 65 yards on 17 carries against Pitt and NC State, including a 9-yard touchdown on his first carry against the Wolfpack, FSU’s lone touchdown in the game. It was his second career touchdown. Meanwhile, on the Gators’ first possession Friday, running back Jadan Baugh will likely break the 1,000-yard mark for the season. Baugh already has 980 yards this season and averages 5.0 yards per carry. Baugh has recorded 8 explosive runs of 20+ yards, including runs of 75, 61, and 53 yards, and has scored 16 rushing TDs this season. UF’s Aaron Philo has firmly established himself as the starting quarterback after alternating with Tramell Jones Jr. earlier in the year. Philo enters on a two-game winning streak following victories over No. 11 Kentucky and Vanderbilt, where he completed 20 of 26 passes for 241 yards with no interceptions and added 73 rushing yards with two touchdowns. Receivers Bailey Stockton and Dallas Wilson are tied with 41 receptions each and a combined 5 receiving TDs. UF’s defense is led by linebacker Myles Graham, son of former NFL running back Earnest Graham, who leads the team with 88 tackles, 4.5 sacks, and 5.5 tackles for loss and returned a fumble 57 yards for a touchdown in last week’s win over Vanderbilt. Some other defensive players whose names we will hear mentioned are LB Aaron Chiles and DE Jayden Woods, who leads the team with 7 sacks and 11 tackles for loss. Last week against NC State, after marching 75 yards in 5 plays on their opening drive to score a touchdown, the Seminoles would only score a field goal in the second quarter, then were shut down and shut out in the second half. FSU was held to 283 total yards, lost the time-of-possession battle by over 13 minutes, and the defense gave up 464 total yards and almost 6 yards per play. Florida State shut out in the second half as Noles fall to NC State One of the few bright spots this season has been FSU kicker Gabe Panikowski, who is 27-for-27 on field goal attempts in his NCAA career, including 12-for-12 this season. He is the only active kicker (min. 15 attempts) in any NCAA division who is perfect in his career, and his 27 consecutive made field goals at the NCAA level is the longest active streak. Last week against NCST, Panikowski connected on a 54-yard field goal, the 7th-longest in FSU history. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. NoleThruandThru (season record: 8-3) As much as I’d love to see a win over those slimy lizards, I’m not going to be fooled again by FSU. At least we had an amazing kicker. An end to 2026 brings a glorious beginning to 2027 and beyond with a whoooooole lot of new faces on and off the field. Go Noles forever and forever and thanks for some fun memories, Stock! UF 31, FSU 20 Jacob Smith (season record: 6-5) It’s come down to this, yet again. This is the second year in a row that game number 12 will decide whether this team makes it to a low to mid-tier bowl game. Florida State’s defense is below average, while UF’s offense is above average. On the other hand, UF’s defense is below average, while FSU’s offense is above average. This could genuinely be the second-highest scoring game of the year. Though, I think UF takes it down the stretch because of all of the injuries on defense the Seminoles are dealing with. If I’m wrong, great! I look forward to playing in the Hot Sauce Bowl presented by Frank. Florida 48, FSU 35 Seminole Uprising (season record: 7-4) It is the dawn of a new day in Tallahassee with the hiring of Glenn Schumann this week. But, as the saying goes, it is always darkest before dawn. One last time, we have to experience the Mike Norvell era as the injury-riddled Seminoles take on Florida. Two weeks ago, after beating Pitt, I would have said FSU had a chance, but the NCSU game was so bad that it is hard to find the reasons why. Florida will run the ball down Florida State’s throats for the second year in a row, and the offense is not designed to play from behind or explosive enough to take advantage of the Gators’ coverage busts on the back end. For the second year in a row, the Seminoles go 5-7. UF 31, FSU 17 Jon Marchant (season record: 7-4 ) I think it’s safe to say the temporary bump from firing Mike Norvell has won off, and along with all of the injuries on offense this team is a shell of whatever it was earlier this season. The Norvell era wasn’t all bad but there was a lot of bad, and it never quite turned out the way we all wanted it too, Norvell included. I think they’ll play harder in this one similar to how they did vs Miami, but the injuries on offense will probably be too much to overcome. Again though, if there’s any takeaway from the Mike Norvell era it’s that any result, good or bad, was never off the table. Florida 31, FSU 23 Tim Scribble (season record: 7-4 ) I fear that this week’s game will be similar to last year’s result. The Florida State defense will be unable to stop UF running back Jadan Baugh. Expect a lot of yards on the ground for the Gators to officially close the Mike Norvell era. UF 35, FSU 20 Matt Minnick (season record: 7-4, ATS: 7-4) Man, I am so tired of losing rivalry games. I just don’t see how FSU will get UF off the field on third downs. And with so many injuries on offense, I don’t see how FSU will score beyond a random explosive play. The only way FSU hangs tough is by winning the turnover battle by a big margin, and that’s tough to do when your QB leads the country in INTs. UF 35, FSU 16 Curt Weiler (season record: 7-4, ATS: 3-8) Hard to shake my belief that this will be the third time in six years Florida denies FSU a bowl bid. The Gators haven’t been an incredible team all season but their highs have been much higher than Florida State’s. Florida 31, Florida State 20 Frank DNole (season record: 5-6) If you look at the Florida State vs. Florida head-to-head comparison chart above, you will notice that the Gators hold the statistical advantage over the Noles in almost every category. Normally, that might be the recipe for a Seminole defeat. However, this week we experienced a full moon that is now in the waning gibbous phase. Not only was it a full moon, but it was also a supermoon, and most importantly, it was a Full Beaver Moon (look it up). What all this means is that the Seminoles will win the offensive, defensive, and special-teams battles because the FSU players will give 115% more effort, they will want it more, and the Noles will play with more heart than their more talented turdly opponent. FSU Seminoles 34, FFFFF 31 P erry Kostidakis (season record: 6-5, 5-6 ATS) I really can’t tell you why I’m going with this choice other than pure delusion, but I have a weird feeling about this game. Here’s a fun fact: interim coaches have gone 3-1 in the series since 2017 (well, I guess technically 3-2, since the 2017 matchup was a matchup of two interims). Two of those wins were on the UF end, but if we’re talking delusion, why not warp some stats in favor of the home team? FSU has shed two streaks (last road win, last Friday win) that were defined by a win over the Gators this season since Rick Stockstill took over, so in the interest of the rule of threes, why not finally earn bowl eligibility with a season-ending victory over the boys from Hogtown? Again, this is a feeling borne out of nothing other than an inkling, since everything on paper and on film says UF should win this one with no issues. Jaden Baugh seems to take particular joy in the rivalry, which doesn’t bode well for an FSU defense that struggles against a lot, but especially against the run. FSU is stumbling in this health-wise, the high-flying feelings of go 2-0 to the Norvell era seemingly washed away by NC State. And unless Tre Wisner has made a turnaround on being healthy, Florida State is going to have to win this on the arm of Ashton Daniels, which the cope glass-half-full way of looking at it is that he has a penchant for performing in rivalry matchups. The only non-delusional, non-anything-can-happen-in-a-rivalry-game reasons I have for thinking that FSU is capable of pulling off a win is that 1) UF has played down to its opponents all season long and 2) the Gators are vulnerable on defense, especially through the air. But brother, it’s Turkey Day, and if there’s one thing I’m thankful for, it’s me never, ever, ever, ever, ever learning my lesson. It was on 3 DEC 1977, on a snowy television at one of my MANY childhood homes; my dad was in the Army, and we lived near Choctawhatchee Beach between Niceville and Freeport, FL. We had to turn our antenna with a pair of channel locks to bring in one of three available channels. I came across this game, and being in love with football at that age, I kept the channel tuned. I was a big Steelers fan then and was more inclined to the NFL. BUT this is when I REALLY became aware of college football. Of course, I noticed those gold helmets with the Spears on the side and immediately fell in love with Florida State. The Noles went on to win that game in Hogtown 37-9, and it was their first win in the series in a decade. I was hooked. I graduated from my beloved university, and my last game as an actual student was the “Choke at Doak”. Friends and I had the opportunity to complete the victory and attend the “5th Quarter in the French Quarter” Sugar Bowl before I went off to my own 22-year Army career. But I digress… Aside from the loss to NCST, this past week has been a GREAT week for FSU generally and the football program specifically. I am hoping and praying the football team takes heart and rises above all the injuries and last week’s loss and can pull out a victory and get bowl-eligible. They deserve it. away.headline: FSU QB Ashton Daniels leaves Florida game injured
away.blurb: Florida State Seminoles starting quarterback Ashton Daniels left FSU's game against the Florida Gators with an apparent injury in the third quarter. Daniels returned to the field on the next possession. Daniels ran for 18 yards on 3rd-and-one but collided with Florida cornerback Cormani McClain at the end of the play. Daniels stumbled when he stood up and had to be helped to the sideline, where he went into the medical tent. He was replaced by Kevin Sperry, who led FSU to a touchdown, making it a 17-10 Florida lead with 3:01 left in the third quarter. Sperry has now played in five games this year, completing five of his seven passes for 30 yards and one touchdown. Daniels has started all 12 games for FSU this season, completing 59.0% of his passes for 2,515 yards, 14 touchdowns, and 14 interceptions. He was 11 of 17 for 110 yards before his injury. He has also ran the ball 14 times for 32 yards. Follow us @FSUWire on X and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Florida State news, notes, and opinions. home.blurb: Philo's run set Florida up at the Seminoles' 13-yard line. The Gators scored three plays later, with Philo's backup, Tramell Jones Jr., getting in the end zone from one yard out to extend his team's lead to 14, 17-3, with 10:55 remaining in the third quarter. With his team driving early in the third quarter with a 10-3 lead, Gators quarterback Aaron Philo went down and remained on the turf after withstanding a hard hit at the end of a 37-yard run against Florida State on Friday, Nov. 27 at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, Florida . Here's the latest on Philo's injury: After enduring the hit, Philo was eventually helped up, left the field and headed to his team's locker room for further evaluation. In the immediate aftermath of the play, it was unclear whether it was a head or shoulder injury Philo had suffered. He later returned to the Florida sideline in street clothes, signaling his day is done. The Georgia Tech transfer, who's in his first year with the program, dealt with a shoulder injury earlier in the season that he suffered in a 38-19 loss to South Carolina on Oct. 10. The injury caused him to miss the Gators' Oct. 17 win at Texas. Heading into Saturday's Week 13 game against Florida State , Philo had completed 70.9% of his passes for 1,727 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions this season, along with 76 rushing attempts for 280 yards and six touchdowns.

The No. 20 Florida Gators (7-4, 5-4 SEC) will take a two-game win streak into the matchup after beating Vanderbilt 34-27 at The Swamp. Florida is 39-28 (two ties) all-time in the series and has won two straight against the Seminoles, including a 40-21 win over FSU in The Swamp last season. In that game, Florida running back Jadan Baugh rushed for 266 yards on 38 carries and 2 TDs to surpass 1,000 yards for the 2025 season. The 6-foot-1, 225-poound Baugh is at 980 yards and 16 TDs this season and is 20 yards shy of becoming the first running back in history to post back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons. Florida football vs FSU prediction Florida 31, Florida State 17: Expect another heavy dose of Jadan Baugh, who will surpass the 1,000-yard mark and rush for more than 100 yards for the first time since Sept. 26 to lead UF to the lopsided win. Florida will control the game on the ground and force a takeaway or two on defense to take its third straight the series and second straight in Tallahassee. Florida football vs FSU key matchup Florida State RB Jadan Baugh vs FSU front seven : Baugh rushed for 266 yards and 2 TDs against the Seminoles and could have another big day against an FSU run defense that's allowing 171.0 yards per game. Expect Florida to give the ball to Baugh early and often in what could be his final game in a UF uniform. Entering Friday's game, Jones went 73 of 111 passing for 712 yards, four touchdowns, and five interceptions while adding 90 yards and a score on the ground. It remains to be seen how severe Philo's injury is from Friday. Philo missed a couple of games earlier in the season due to a shoulder injury. His status is unclear before the Gators head into bowl season, when they'll have an opportunity for a dozen or so practices before their final game. picks.headline: Three last-minute Wisconsin football vs. Minnesota predictions
picks.blurb: Three last-minute Wisconsin football vs. Minnesota predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games NBA Cup: Knockouts set Friday's college football scores Steelers dominate without Rodgers Luka shoved by fan USWNT qualifies for 2027 World Cup Three last-minute Wisconsin football vs. Minnesota predictions Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Wisconsin Badgers have the chance to end the 2026 campaign on a high note if they are able to take down the Minnesota Golden Gophers and move to 8-4. By no means would it be a storied season that goes down in the record books, but it should be enough to keep Fickell from any more serious conversations about his job security. That being said, all that momentum would cease if Wisconsin were to lose to Minnesota, and knowing how inconsistent Wisconsin has been this season, there aren't many things you can bank on. However, we take our best cracks at three predictions below. No. 1: Wisconsin loses the turnover battle None of these predictions will come off as hot takes by any means, but perhaps this is the most levelheaded take on this list. On the season, the Badgers sit 80th in turnover margin at -2 against FBS competition. Minnesota, on the other hand, is 14th-best in the nation at a +7 margin. No. 2 Wisconsin's rushing offense is responsible for each of their touchdowns As previously mentioned, the Badgers are inconsistent this season, and usually when the offense looks like it has something figured out, the next week it falls apart. Well, last week the Badgers' offense ran for 381 yards across 51 total carries that involved two 100+ yard runners in Colton Joseph and Darrion Dupree. That being said, Minnesota's pass defense against FBS competition ranks 35th-best in the country, allowing 196.6 yards through the air. Their rushing defense, meanwhile, sits No. 74 in the country at 154.4 yards. If Wisconsin's offense is productive, it likely comes on the ground. No. 3 The two teams do not combine for 600 yards of total offense All that needs to be said here is that the Badgers and the Gophers each have a top-50 defense against FBS competition (Wisconsin 5th, Minnesota 42nd) while also posting total offenses that rank 118th and 131st. Taylor has dealt with injury again this year, and his production has bottomed out. Coming into the contest against Northwestern, he had just 295 yards on 110 carries. Despite six touchdowns, his 2.7 yards per carry was easily a career low. The offense has been anemic for Minnesota all season, and problems on the offensive line have certainly crushed the running game. Still, Taylor has not looked like the same player from earlier in his career. It makes sense that he would return for a fifth year if there is any hope he can flash enough to play at the next level. He played in six games as a freshman in 2023, too many to redshirt under the old rules, but the NCAA's new eligibility rules give him a path to a fifth season in 2027. After the game, Taylor was asked about sitting out the senior ceremony and what comes next. He didn't tip his hand either way, saying he is focused on the rest of this season, with Wisconsin and a bowl game still ahead. picks.blurb: Predicting Final Score of Michigan Football vs. Ohio State Skip to main content SI.COM MORE SPORTS NEWS SI.COM WOLVERINES FB SI.COM WOLVERINES BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Game. Michigan vs. Ohio State . Buckeyes vs. Wolverines . It's the best rivalry in all of football and it's here. But it's not the normal game. Neither team is doing anything special with its postseason plans. The Wolverines nor the Buckeyes are headed to the Big Ten title game, nor does either team have a spot in the playoff. Instead, both teams are bowl-eligible, and as bad as Michigan's season has been, a win over the Buckeyes and Ohio State will have the same record as the Wolverines this season— 7-5. But Michigan will have to play another good game in order to pull off back-to-back upsets after taking down UCLA last weekend in triple overtime. Here's how Michigan on SI sees the game going. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Michigan's defense can go into Columbus and win the game against Ohio State. The Wolverines' defense has kept them in every game this season, aside from a second-half blunder against Oregon. The problem is Michigan's offense. We've seen 11 games from this unit and nothing really gets better. Michigan's defense can go into Columbus and win the game against Ohio State. The Wolverines' defense has kept them in every game this season, aside from a second-half blunder against Oregon. The problem is Michigan's offense. We've seen 11 games from this unit and nothing really gets better. Savion Hiter ran for over 100 yards in the last two games, so there are some silver lining. And Ohio State's defense hasn't been good in the last four games. But the Buckeyes will have the best player on the field in Jeremiah Smith, who will be hard to defend. This game is 100% winnable for Michigan, but I haven't seen enough from the Wolverines' offense to believe they can make enough plays to pull off another upset . Final score: Ohio State 17, Michigan 13 Justice Steiner This is one of the least anticipated versions of ‘The Game’ we have seen in recent memory. Ohio State is on the decline since starting QB Julian Sayin went down with an injury. But it does feel like both coaches are fighting to keep their jobs. If Michigan wants to win, they need to contain Jeremiah Smith the best they can and get Savion Hiter going in the run game. Also, continuing to get the tight ends involved like they did last week will be big for the UofM offense, something they haven’t done most of the season. Although I believe Michigan has a chance and the game will be close, I don’t trust them to pick up the win on the road. The best unit on the field will be Michigan’s defense, but Michigan’s offense will also be the worst unit on the field. I think the overall balance of the Buckeyes will be too much for Michigan to handle in this one. If Ohio State is motivated, and I have no reason to believe they won't be, the Buckeyes could roll. Final score: Ohio State 16, Michigan 3 Jacob Westendorf Ohio State is not what they usually are at this point of the year. A trip to Columbus has resembled more of a death march prior to 2022. This Ohio State team is not as good as any of the iterations Michigan has played since then. The Wolverine defense is good enough to keep them in the game. Jay Hill says he has a plan for Jeremiah Smith. The plan only goes so far. At some point, Ohio State's playmakers will just make one too many plays against Michigan's defense The Wolverine offense, which was still bad last week, will struggle again as the season ends at 6-6 with a narrow Buckeye victory in Columbus. Jason B. Hirschhorn From a playoff perspective, Saturday's matchup between Michigan and Ohio State lacks juice. The Wolverines fell completely out of the playoff discourse back in October, and the Buckeyes did the same after losing three of their last four games. And yet, the 2026 edition of The Game holds tremendous stakes for both sides. With another loss, Ohio State will exceed its total from the last two years combined and tie for its most in a single season with a non-interim head coach since 2001. Such a result could cost Ryan Day his job. On the other side, Michigan needs a win to avoid finishing a non-truncated regular season with a non-winning record for the first time since the Brady Hoke era. If Kyle Whittingham has any hope of surviving 2026, he'll need the political capital that comes with a victory over the Wolverines' archrivals. If star players determine the outcome, the Buckeyes have the advantage. Superstar wideout and Heisman front-runner Jeremiah Smith provides instant offense, and even the best teams struggle to contain him. However, if the Wolverines' defense can fluster freshman quarterback Luke Fahey and come up with a key turnover or two à la Chris Bracy's acrobatic interception against UCLA, they have a chance. Ultimately, slowing down Smith long enough for Michigan's lackluster offense to capitalize on the other end seems too big of an ask. Skip to main content SI.COM MORE SPORTS NEWS SI.COM WOLVERINES FB SI.COM WOLVERINES BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Game is here . Tomorrow, Michigan will face Ohio State in a game that unfortunately does not mean as much as it has for each of the last 10 years. Neither team is playing for anything significant. The Wolverines are going to be bowl eligible after last week’s win over UCLA. This week’s game is mor e about pride, and bragging rights. Those still matter, even in this day in age. Here are our predictions for The Game Jeremiah Smith is Good, not Great Jay Hill says he has a plan. That’s a good start against someone as good as Jeremiah Smith. Smith, however, is going to make plays at some point. Smith was pretty quiet in the team’s 13-10 loss to Michigan in 2024. He had just three catches for 40 yards and a touchdown last year, but the Buckeyes took the air out of the ball for most of the second half. The reality, however, is that Smith has never had a game-breaking performance against the Wolverines. That will continue against them this week. Hill’s plan will be to take Smith out of the game as much as a defense is able to do so. Smith will still make his plays, but fall short of his averages of 7.8 catches and 135 yards. Mason Bonner Continues Ascension Mason Bonner looked like a weapon who was starting to emerge last week for Michigan’s offense. He scored their only touchdown of the game on a contested catch from Bryce Underwood after a forced fumble was recovered deep in UCLA territory. No. 21 Ohio State looks to win a second straight game over Michigan when the Buckeyes host the Wolverines at Ohio Stadium in Columbus, Ohio, on Saturday at noon ET (FOX). Despite Michigan's upset win last week, my college football picks back the Buckeyes as 10.5-point favorites (77% moneyline probability) in a low-scoring game on Saturday, Nov. 28. Michigan is in a massive letdown spot after ending UCLA's undefeated season last week, and Wolverines coach Kyle Whittingham continually puts his foot in his mouth , especially about this rivalry . The Buckeyes have a clear offensive advantage against a Michigan team ranked 96th in offensive success rate (41.8%) . Ohio State QB Luke Fahey had his best game of the season last week (95.0 QBR vs. Nebraska ) and is throwing to Jeremiah Smith , the Heisman Trophy odds favorite. Given the QB situation for both teams, I'd play the Under as low as 35.5 . The Wolverines rank 117th in early-down EPA per play and 124th in available yards percentage (38.2%). Their offensive ineptitude has led them to hit the Under in nine of 11 games this season , including every game against defense ranked top 100 by SP+ . But Ohio State won't light up the scoreboard either. Michigan's defense ranks top 10 nationally in success rate (37.4%) and has allowed more than 21 points in only one game this season. Michigan vs Ohio State combo Though this is the headliner of our Top 25 predictions because of the gravity of this rivalry, Michigan is in worse shape than Ohio State in a down year for both teams, and 'The Game' won't be close. The Wolverines have a checked-out coach, distractions with the botched hiring of an athletic director, and one of the worst offenses in the Power Four ( ranked No. 108 by SP+ ). While Fahey isn't the most talented QB, he's better than Underwood, and Smith is the X-factor in what will be a game short on offense. Smith leads the country in both receiving yards (1,482) and receiving TDs (17) , and he will be the difference in the second half. picks.blurb: Urban Meyer’s Ohio State-Michigan prediction comes with a caveat that may concern Buckeyes fans - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games NBA Cup: Knockouts set Friday's college football scores Steelers dominate without Rodgers Luka shoved by fan USWNT qualifies for 2027 World Cup Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Urban Meyer is picking Ohio State to beat Michigan on Saturday, which will surprise nobody who remembers his 7-0 record against the Wolverines as the Buckeyes' head coach. He made the call while speaking on stage at an event, in video Adam King of 10TV posted Sunday, and the Ohio State team he picked arrives at The Game in a place it has rarely been. The Buckeyes are 7-4 after a 31-28 loss at Nebraska, their fourth defeat of the season and their third in four weeks, following losses at USC and at home to Oregon. Their College Football Playoff hopes are gone, and they are unranked in the Coaches Poll for the first time since 2011. Julian Sayin has been sidelined since hurting his right arm against Indiana on Oct. 17, which has left true freshman Luke Fahey at quarterback. Former Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Urban Meyer salutes the fans chanting his name during the College Football Playoff quarterfinal against the Oregon Ducks at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, Calif. on Jan. 1, 2025. Ohio State won 41-21. Michigan, at 6-5, comes in off the biggest win of Kyle Whittingham's first season. The Wolverines beat previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA 18-16 in triple overtime on Saturday, Whittingham's 67th birthday, when Bryce Underwood found Jalen Hoffman for the deciding two-point conversion. Where Meyer sees The Game being won "The roster's better for Ohio State, but the best unit right now playing is the Wolverine defense, and that concerns me a little bit. They really hammered UCLA. You gotta think the other side of the ball for the Wolverines is terrible, they're last in the country. And so to still have decent numbers, only one team's scored over 21 points on them, Oregon. So that's a legit defense. On offense, we got the best player in the country, maybe the best player to ever play college football. That's how good Jeremiah is. But we also have a backup quarterback, the offensive line's not playing great, so I think this is gonna be a rock fight, a low-scoring game. I think whoever punches the hardest is gonna win the game. I expect it to be a 17-10, 17-14 game, and I've got the Buckeyes," Meyer said. In early October, Meyer called the 2026 Wolverines a "train wreck." Hearing him now rank their defense above every unit Ohio State has is about as clear a measure as any of how far the Buckeyes have fallen in a month. Urban Meyer came to love star quarterback Braxton Miller (5) and the rest of the 2012 Buckeyes, and to this day does not understand why they were punished for NCAA violations committed by predecessors. His case for Ohio State rests almost entirely on Jeremiah Smith, and the Nebraska loss showed what that version of the offense looks like with Fahey running it. The freshman's best moment in Lincoln was a 67-yard touchdown to Smith down the field. If Michigan's defense is as good as Meyer says, the Buckeyes may not get many clean shots like that, and a 17-14 game decided by a handful of throws to one receiver is a thin margin for a team that has already lost four times. Ryan Day was asked after the Nebraska loss if he still had confidence in defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, and he steered the answer straight to Michigan. "We don't have a choice. We've got to get this thing together next week to go win this game," Day said . Michigan and Ohio State kick off at noon ET Saturday at Ohio Stadium on Fox. Here are our predictions for the game: Ohio State vs. Michigan predictions Joey Kaufman, Columbus Dispatch: Michigan 24, Ohio State 20 : It's felt like fool's gold in recent weeks to pick Ohio State to end its late-season slide, so there's hesitation to pull that lever. Michigan's offensive futility should make it easy to go chalk with the Buckeyes . It averages the second-fewest points per game among Power 4 teams and has vacillated between starting Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr at quarterback. But the Wolverines don't need to score much with a suffocating defense. They also have a bit of momentum after an upset of unbeaten UCLA last weekend. The vibes just seem better in Ann Arbor, which might matter the most with only bragging right at stake. Rob Oller, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 17, Michigan 16 : I went back and forth on this one before deciding that Michigan's offense is simply too anemic to pull off a win in Ohio Stadium. The Wolverines rank 130th in first downs, 128th in passing yards and 99th in rushing yardage per game. On the flip side, UM's defense, ranked ninth nationally, is the most reliable piece on either team, so if the Wolverines can hold OSU to 14 points they have a great chance at winning in Columbus for a third straight time. It likely comes down to which team's head and heart are into a game where the only thing on the line is bragging rights. Brianna Mac Kay, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 21, Michigan 17 : Ohio State's offense with Luke Fahey at quarterback has shown flashes of promise, primarily before the defense put the Buckeyes in a deficit across the past four games. If the defense can keep Michigan under its season average of 18.3 points per game, which ranks 129th in the country, the offense should be able to put together enough momentum to finish the season with a win over the Wolverines. Dan Aulbach, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 17, Michigan 13 : We finally get to see what happens when a stoppable force meets a moveable object. On the one hand, Michigan has the same starting quarterback as last year's edition of the rivalry, but Bryce Underwood has severely underperformed his expectations. Michigan's offense is lethargic, but Ohio State's defense has allowed 30-plus points in three of its last four games. Michigan's defense is elite (ninth in scoring defense), but so is Jeremiah Smith . The Buckeyes proved earlier in the year they can play and win against a defense-first team in Iowa, so I'll reluctantly pick the Buckeyes. Ohio State will have one last opportunity to meet a goal this season. The College Football Playoff is gone, so too is the shot at its first Big Ten title since 2019. All that's left is a chance to beat arch-rival Michigan in 'The Game' on Saturday. Each week of the Ohio State football season, we like to ask our writers to predict a final score and a quick synopsis of what will happen with that week's game, so why not lean into this one, the biggest game on the schedule every year, according to some. Here's what Phil, Mark, and Alec say about Ohio State vs. Michigan in 'The Game' Saturday. Ohio State vs. Michigan prediction, according to Phil Harrison, Lead Writer/Editor It won't be pretty. Michigan's defense is too good for that, and Ohio State's offense hasn't been consistent enough to expect a blowout. But the Buckeyes have the best player on the field, the home crowd, and a Michigan offense that can't score enough to keep up. Ohio State grinds one out, Day gets his first home win over Michigan, and the Buckeyes head into bowl season with something to feel good about. Score Prediction: Ohio State 20, Michigan 17 Ohio State vs. Michigan prediction, according to Mark Russell, Featured Writer For the first time in a long time, pride is the only thing on the line for The Game. Urban Meyer said it best earlier this week. Michigan's offense is pathetic, and yet the Wolverines have been in every game. Why? Because the defense is really good. I'm comforted a bit that Ohio State managed to put up 28 points against a very good Nebraska defense. If the Michigan offense had any kind of pulse, my pick might be different. I do think the Wolverines will have some success running the ball, but I think the Buckeyes can do just enough on the offensive side to come out on top. Ohio State vs. Michigan, according to Alec Lasley, Featured Writer It all comes down to this - one game to salvage some part of the season, a year that has gone entirely differently than anticipated. The urgency and attention to detail have been nowhere near where they need to be, and that can't happen this weekend. Luke Fahey has progressed nicely in recent weeks, but that hasn't helped OSU's failing defense since its bye week. Can the Buckeyes put together their first complete performance in nearly a month? I'm not sure a complete performance will happen, but I think OSU does just enough to come out on top. Wolverines Football Updated: Nov. 24, 2026, 9:28 a.m. | Published: Nov. 23, 2026, 11:55 a.m. Aaron McMann | amcmann@mlive.com ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Kyle Whittingham said Monday morning that Michigan football would be sticking with Bryce Underwood at quarterback this week. Given what happened over the weekend, the Wolverines’ upset win over No. 4 UCLA, 18-16, in overtime, it makes sense. The sophomore didn’t put up impressive numbers, but did enough to help the team -- and completed the game-winning two-point conversion throw. “Bryce is the guy,” Whittingham told reporters ahead of Saturday’s rivalry showdown at Ohio State (12 p.m., FOX). “Bryce is the guy and Tommy (Carr) is the No. 2.” Whittingham did add a stipulator, calling it the plan “barring any(thing) unforeseen” like “getting dinged up in practice or something like that. “That’s how it will be,” Whittingham continued. Roughly 45 minutes later, CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reported that Underwood suffered a lower-body injury in the win over UCLA that left his status in question for Saturday’s game. Soon after, national reporters from On3 and ESPN confirmed the injury to Underwood. The quarterback appeared fine physically as he spoke to the press after the game on Saturday, calling it “a blessing” to get a second chance at being the Wolverines’ starting quarterback. Michigan will be required to submit a player availability report to the Big Ten beginning on Wednesday, with updates expected daily leading up to Saturday’s game in Columbus. RELATED: Michigan football a double-digit underdog vs. Ohio State In seven starts this season, Underwood has completed 54 percent of his throws for 1,077 yards and six touchdowns, with six interceptions and two fumbles lost. Turnovers got him benched during a Week 6 win over Penn State, opening the door for freshman Tommy Carr to take over.

Does it really matter all that much on a national scale? Yeah, it's getting stronger thanks to the consistent success of head coach Jeff Brohm at Louisville, and with Will Stein turning Kentucky into a rising power. The Wildcats might have slipped out of the CFP Top 25, but they've been in the mix over the last several weeks. Louisville is currently No. 19, and it might be the best ACC team available in the bowl process. Louisville vs Kentucky: Quick Hits Louisville has won six straight since losing back-to-back ACC games in late September. The 30-27 loss to Wake Forest was the difference between playing for the ACC Championship and finishing third in the conference. Kentucky started 7-1 but lost three straight. It's a win a way from this being the program's best season since 2021. Louisville won 41-0 last year, but Kentucky is 5-2 in the last seven meetings. How To Watch Louisville vs Kentucky Date: Saturday, November 28, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN2 Location: Kroger Field, Lexington, KY – Week 13 Schedule, Game Previews – CFP and Bowl Projections Why Louisville Will Win Kentucky has stopped scoring. The offense wasn't horrible in last week's 28-14 loss to Missouri, and the passing attack wasn't awful in the loss to Tennessee, but the ground attack was stuffed by Florida, and the three turnovers against both the Vols and Tigers were a killer. Louisville's offense has been solid over the second half of the season, but it's the attacking defense that's taking over games. The Cardinals have forced 13 turnovers over their six-game winning run. Why Kentucky Will Win The Wildcats have to start taking the ball away again. That was part of the puzzle when the team was rolling, with 18 takeaways in the first eight games. There has been just one over this last three-game losing streak. Start forcing mistakes again, and the overall production will follow. UK quarterback Kenny Minchey has to crank up the big plays. All three Louisville losses came when the defense got hit by a slew of deep shots – Wake Forest, NC State, and Ole Miss all averaged over nine yards per throw. Louisville vs Kentucky Prediction, Betting Lines Kentucky has the talent, coaching, and experience to pull this off after losing the last two years by a combined score of 82-14. It's far better this season, but Louisville is too sharp, with too good a running game to be slowed to a crawl. It'll be a good, entertaining game, but Kentucky won't be able to score enough – it's 0-4 when scoring fewer than 21. It takes 30 to beat the Cardinals as the rivalry enters a new phase. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Louisville picks, odds for Governor's Cup football game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games NBA Cup: Knockouts set Friday's college football scores Steelers dominate without Rodgers Luka shoved by fan USWNT qualifies for 2027 World Cup Kentucky vs. Louisville picks, odds for Governor's Cup football game Alexis Cubit and Ryan Black, Louisville Courier Journal · The Courier Journal Fri, November 27, 2026 at 10:09 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the first time, the annual Governor's Cup rivalry football game will be a top-25 clash between Kentucky and Louisville . The No. 18 Cardinals continued to climb in the rankings thanks to six straight wins heading into the regular-season finale after a commanding win over Pitt. UofL's defense held the Panthers to a season-low 10 points , while Cards quarterback Lincoln Kienholz had a career-best five touchdowns in the 32-point triumph . In doing so, Kienholz joined Lamar Jackson as the only Cards quarterbacks to throw 20 or more touchdown passes and rush for 10 or more touchdowns in the same season. Kienholz enters the Governor's Cup with 20 TD passes and 11 scoring runs. Meanwhile, the No. 25 Wildcats have steadily dropped in the polls because of a three-game losing streak to end SEC play. In Will Stein's head coaching debut, the Cats started league action on a high note and appeared to be on their way to Atlanta for the SEC championship game. But UK was outscored by a combined 83-34 in consecutive losses to Tennessee, Florida and Missouri. Turnovers and empty red-zone trips spelled trouble for Kentucky in its most recent loss, a 28-14 defeat against the Tigers. But the squad is looking to salvage the season with a win over the rival Cardinals. Can Louisville make it three straight wins over Kentucky, or will the Wildcats spoil the regular-season finale for the Cards? Here's what The Courier Journal's college reporters and columnist think. Stream Louisville vs. Kentucky football Kentucky vs. Louisville odds, moneyline, over/under Odds courtesy of BetMGM, as of Friday, Nov. 27 . Moneyline: Louisville -140; Kentucky +115 Spread: Louisville by 2.5 Over/under: 54.5 Kentucky vs. Louisville scouting report Why Kentucky has an advantage: Comparing the teams side by side, the Cats have an edge statistically in several areas. But UK's most notable advantage is keeping laundry off the field. Kentucky ranks among the top two in the SEC (and the top 20 in the FBS) this season in both fewest total penalties and fewest penalty yards. Louisville is nowhere close to that in either department. With the Wildcats lacking upper hands elsewhere, their discipline is one area they should be able to hang their hat on this weekend. Why Louisville has an advantage: Louisville comes into the Governor's Cup with one of the most high-powered offenses in the country. The Cardinals are averaging 38.6 points, which ranks eighth among FBS programs, and 462.8 total yards of offense, 12th-most nationally. Kienholz is coming off one of his best games of the season after throwing a career-high five touchdown passes in a dominant win over Pitt. He also has a strong group of talented receivers around him and two explosive running backs beside him. But the Cards' six-game winning streak is equally due to their defense showing great improvement and getting pressure on opposing quarterbacks. Louisville's defense comes into the Week 13 contest averaging 4.3 sacks per game over the past three contests. That included a season-high six sacks against North Carolina two weeks ago. Kentucky vs. Louisville predictions, picks for college football Week 13 Louisville 30, Kentucky 27. A banged-up Kentucky team will put forth a valiant effort. The Cats will have the entire weight of a frenzied Kroger Field behind them. But the momentum that saw UK win six straight games and debut at No. 6 in the College Football Playoff ranking at one point this season has disappeared. The hosts lose a heartbreaker at home as the Cards notch their third consecutive win in the rivalry. Louisville 35, Kentucky 31. The Cardinals will secure a fourth consecutive nine-win season and increase their winning streak over the Wildcats after catching fire during the latter half of the season. A high-powered offense and much-improved defense will spell trouble for Will Stein and his stumbling Wildcats squad in Stein's first game on the other side of the Governor's Cup rivalry. Brooks Holton Louisville 31, Kentucky 27. It's pretty simple: The Cards have won six in a row entering the regular-season finale, while the Cats have dropped three straight. Give me the hotter team. Louisville 32, Kentucky 24. For as well as the Wildcats' season started, I still think the Cards have their number. A noon kick down the road with the streaks each team is riding now? Yeah, I'll take Louisville. Louisville 20, Kentucky 17. UofL comes into the game with a lot of momentum, but whenever it seems one-sided in this rivalry, the underdog usually shows a lot of fight. Carson Hilbert adds his name in rivalry lore with a last-second field goal to win it for the Cards. Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads If rivalry bragging rights were not enough motivation for Kentucky football in the battle for the Governor's Cup this week, the stakes are even higher for Will Stein's team. After three straight losses, Kentucky dropped out of the top 25 rankings from both the Associated Press and College Football Playoff committee this week. Beating No. 19 Louisville would stop that slide, making it clear that Stein's first season was a success even after falling out of playoff contention. A victory would give Kentucky eight regular season wins for just the fourth time since 1977. With so much crossover between the two programs this season, managing the rivalry emotions could be key. Here is what you need to know entering the game. Familiar faces Stein will get most of the attention as he coaches against his alma mater for the first time, but he is far from the only key figure who has switched sides in the rivalry. UK general manager Pete Nochta, tight ends coach Justin Burke, running backs coach Kolby Smith and assistant running backs coach Keith Towbridge also played at Louisville. Director of football sports performance Brandon Roberts, passing game coordinator Andrew Coverdale and assistant strength coach Joe Midday previously coached at Louisville. Kentucky wide receiver and punt returner Brock Coffman played his freshman season at U of L. "Nowadays it's a business, so you have to make the right decision," Coffman said earlier this year. "What's going to benefit you the most? I feel like I've been on the right path that's going to benefit me the best way." Six Louisville players started their careers at UK: wide receiver Montavin Quisenberry, defensive lineman Jerod Smith, linebacker Jacob Smith, cornerback DJ Waller, center Evan Wibberley and defensive lineman Tommy Ziesmer. They were all recruited to Louisville as transfers by Vince Marrow, who spent more than a decade as the recruiting coordinator for Mark Stoops at UK. Former Kentucky staffer Chase Heuke is also on the front office staff at Louisville. Of the former Wildcats, Wibberley has played the largest role for Louisville this season, starting eight of the first 11 games. Waller and Jerod Smith have each started three games for the Louisville defense. Smith has recorded 20 tackles, 4.5 tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks. Waller has 17 tackles and one pass breakup. Kentucky Wildcats running back Jovantae Barnes (2) could start against Louisville if CJ Baxter and Jason Patterson are unavailable. (Ryan C. Hermens/rhermens@herald-leader.com) Kentucky football injury report UK will not release a public injury report this week since the SEC rule applies to only conference games. There are several injury situations to watch in pregame warmups, though, after right tackle Malachi Wood and running backs CJ Baxter and Jason Patterson left the Missouri game earlier due to injuries. "I would say it's day to day on those guys right now," Stein said Monday. "I wouldn't say it's a complete like they're going to play. I would say the closer we get, it'll be more of a game-time decision. I'm hoping we can get them back. That'd be huge news for us. Obviously, I think people saw what the injuries looked like. They're going through the protocol to try to get themselves back to play this week." Baxter has battled injuries throughout the second half of the season, so his return Saturday would be a surprise. That would leave Patterson (if he is available) and Jovantae Barnes as the top two running backs. Barnes has performed well at times, but he has lost two fumbles in key moments during the losing streak. Kentucky vs. Louisville prediction Louisville is a bad matchup for the version of Kentucky on display the past three games. The Cardinals are tied for 17th nationally in passing plays of at least 20 yards (45) and rank eighth in points per game (38.6). How much of that is a product of a weaker ACC schedule and how much can be duplicated in Kroger Field? There are recent examples of Kentucky looking far better in the rivalry game than it did in SEC play, but I need to see this team fix its recent issues before picking it to win. picks.headline: Kentucky vs Louisville: Final thoughts, prediction
picks.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
picks.blurb: Kentucky football faces Louisville in a highly anticipated Governor's Cup with two former legendary quarterbacks at Trinity high school on opposing sidelines. This is Will Stein's first Governor's Cup as a head coach, and he has had a phenomenal year one with the Wildcats. Jeff Brohm is leading the Cardinals and is trying to keep the trophy in Louisville for a third straight year, after back-to-back dominant wins in this series over the past two seasons. Kentucky really needs this one to avoid a winless November after the incredible 7-1 start to the season. We previewed Louisville's explosive offense and their defense that has struggled in a lot of areas this year. This game has a clear cut shootout potential, and I would expect a fun back-and-forth type of game tomorrow at Kroger Field. The stakes are high, as Louisville just flipped four-star defensive back commit Tristin Hughes from Kentucky earlier in the week. Hughes was one of the highest rated commits of Will Stein's first recruiting class, so this really set the tone for rivalry week. This is exactly why a lot is at stake, these two staffs have a ton of crossover and will be going head-to-head in recruiting for many years to come. Kentucky's Pete Nochta was at Louisville for a long time before joining Will Stein, similar to Vince Marrow joining the Cardinals after a long run with the Wildcats. If you read the tea leaves, these two in particular did not seem to get along in their short time working together at Louisville. With all of that to consider plus the recruiting side of things, we are in for one heated rivalry game tomorrow. Kentucky has to avoid going 0-4 since the bye week, and this is their final opportunity to do so. In this three game losing streak, Kentucky has averaged just 11 points per game and the offense has struggled. Louisville, on the other hand, comes into this game on a six game winning streak after a 2-3 start to the season. The Cardinals are bringing one of the most explosive offenses in the country to Kroger Field. The Cardinals offense is led by signal-caller Lincoln Kienholz, who has a big arm and is extremely physical when he runs the football. Kienholz has a very similar play style to Will Levis when he was at Kentucky. This can pose plenty of problems for the Wildcats defense who recently gave up 100-plus yards on the ground to Florida quarterback Aaron Philo. Kienholz has a dynamic backfield duo as Isaac Brown and Keyjuan Brown both average around seven yards per carry, and wide receiver Tre Richardson can create explosive plays with the blink of an eye. This is a Louisville offense that can score from any area of the field. As much of a task as it will be for the Kentucky defense to slow them down, I believe the taller (and more important) task is for the Wildcats offense to capitalize on their opportunities. Last week, Kentucky scored 14 points and just one touchdown against Missouri despite having seven trips to the red zone. This cannot happen again and Kentucky has to finish drives to win this football game. With all of that said, Louisville is statistically the worst pass defense the Wildcats have faced all season in the FBS. Turnovers will be a huge part of this game, as they always are but this game will come down to Kentucky being able to finish drives. Kentucky will move the ball well on this defense, they did it last week against a much better defense on the road. The key will be finishing drives and taking care of the football; I think Kentucky does that and Will Stein starts off 1-0 in a high scoring Governor's Cup. Prediction: Kentucky 34, Louisville 31 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky vs Louisville: Final thoughts, prediction
