Kentucky vs. Louisville game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction
picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Louisville game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue November 28, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Kentucky hopes to snap a three-game losing streak and avoid losing a third straight game to Louisville. After a great start to the season, with a 7-1 record heading into the bye week and November, Kentucky Football has now lost three straight games. The Wildcats have suffered losses to Tennessee on the road, Florida at home, and most recently Missouri on the road. Heading into the Missouri matchup, Kentucky was ranked No. 16 in the AP Top 25 Poll. However, after a 28-14 loss to the Tigers, the Wildcats have officially fallen out of the rankings. Many Kentucky fans expected the team to bounce back against Florida at home, especially with a sellout crowd at Kroger Field. Unfortunately, the Wildcats came up short on their final drive. Meanwhile, against Missouri, Kentucky had several opportunities to score more than 14 points but struggled to capitalize in the red zone. Sacks, turnovers, and turnovers on downs ultimately prevented the Wildcats from putting more points on the board. While the final three games of the season have not gone well, not many fans expected Kentucky to reach seven wins during Will Stein’s first year, especially considering the difficult schedule the Wildcats faced. Although some fans are disappointed with how the past few weeks have unfolded, many are still pleased with what Stein has accomplished during his first season. Stein has even described the year as successful, despite the possibility of losing to Louisville at home to close out the regular season. Hopefully, that will not be the case. Now, let’s get into the Louisville matchup, as they face off for the Governor’s Cup. Louisville Cardinals (8-3) Kentucky holds the all-time series lead against Louisville, 20-17, but the Wildcats have lost their last two matchups against the Cardinals. Last year, Louisville went on to win 41-0, shutting out Kentucky on the road. That result ultimately contributed to former head coach Mark Stoops being fired. In 2024, the Cardinals also defeated the Wildcats, winning 41-14 at Kroger Field in another disappointing performance for Kentucky. Before that, Kentucky won five straight games against Louisville. Now, Will Stein, who played at Louisville, is leading the Wildcats and will face his former team for the first time as Kentucky’s head coach. As for Louisville, the Cardinals got off to a rocky start, opening the season with a 2-3 record. However, they have since won six consecutive games and improved to 8-3 on the year. A major reason for Louisville’s early struggles was its defense, which had difficulty stopping opposing offenses. Meanwhile, the Cardinals’ offense continued to put up plenty of points, keeping them competitive in several games. Now, things have started to come together for head coach Jeff Brohm and his team. Louisville will look to win its third consecutive game against Kentucky and improve to 9-3 on the season. The Wildcats will certainly have their hands full, as Louisville averages 38.6 points per game, which ranks eighth in the country. The Cardinals also allow 23.4 points per game, ranking 55th nationally. Kentucky will need to find a way to slow down dual-threat quarterback Lincoln Kienholz, who has thrown for 2,739 yards while completing 67.5% of his passes. He has recorded 20 passing touchdowns and four interceptions while also contributing 392 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the ground. In total, Kienholz has accounted for 31 touchdowns this season, making him one of the biggest threats Kentucky will have to contain. Louisville also has two talented running backs, with Isaac Brown leading the way. Brown has recorded 120 carries for 834 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. The Cardinals also rely on Keyjuan Brown, who has totaled 96 carries for 672 yards and six touchdowns. At wide receiver, Louisville has several players who contribute to the passing game, but three have emerged as the team’s primary targets. Tre Richardson leads the group with 58 receptions for 822 receiving yards and five touchdowns. Lawayne McCoy has recorded 36 receptions for 640 yards and six touchdowns, while TreyShun Hurry has added 45 receptions for 542 yards and three touchdowns. As mentioned earlier, Louisville has not been particularly strong defensively this season, but there are a few players Kentucky will need to watch closely. Stanquan Clark leads the Cardinals in tackles with 77, making him one of the team’s most important defensive players. Kentucky will need to find ways to avoid him in space and prevent him from making plays. Defensive lineman Tyler Thompson is another player to watch, as he has recorded 6.5 of Louisville’s 32 sacks this season. That means he is responsible for roughly one-fifth of the team’s total sacks, making him a major threat along the defensive line. Kentucky will also need to take care of the football, as turnovers have become a major concern over the past three games. The Wildcats have committed turnovers in every game since their matchup against Tennessee. Kentucky recorded two fumbles and an interception against the Volunteers, one fumble against Florida, and one fumble along with two interceptions against Missouri. Those numbers are concerning, especially considering Kentucky had only five turnovers before that stretch, including three against Alabama and two against South Alabama. Louisville’s defense has recorded 12 interceptions this season, with defensive back Kaleb Beasley responsible for five of them. Kentucky will need to be especially careful when throwing in his direction. The Cardinals have also forced eight fumbles, meaning the Wildcats will need to protect the football and avoid giving Louisville any extra opportunities. If Kentucky hopes to pull off the upset, it will need to play a clean game, limit turnovers, and find a way to slow down Louisville’s explosive offense. How to watch Louisville Cardinals vs. Kentucky Wildcats Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Date: Saturday, November 28 Time: 12:00 p.m. ET Online streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a +2.5-point underdog after the Wildcats were previously -1.5-point favorites. ESPN win probability: Kentucky has just a 35.6% chance of winning, according to ESPN . Our early prediction: Before the season started, I predicted Kentucky would win six games but lose to Louisville, believing Will Stein would have too much emotion coaching against his former team, where he once played. While Kentucky is currently on a three-game losing streak and sits at 7-4 on the season, Louisville has won six straight games and is now 8-3. Many believe all the momentum is on Louisville’s side, which makes complete sense, especially since several other outlets are now predicting the Cardinals to defeat Kentucky. The Wildcats will need to finish drives and find a way to slow down Louisville’s high-powered offense. Kentucky has shown throughout the season that it can do that at times, including during matchups against South Carolina and LSU. With all of that being said, I believe this game will mirror the 2023 matchup, when Kentucky escaped with a 38-31 victory on the road. Although this year’s game will be played at Kroger Field, I believe the Wildcats will pull off another victory in a high-scoring contest. Kentucky will close out the regular season with an 8-4 record, solidifying what I believe has been a magnificent first season under Stein. Final score: Kentucky 34, Louisville 27. picks.headline: How Kentucky football and No. 19 Louisville match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey (68.1% completions, 2,448 yards, 15 touchdowns vs. four interceptions) threw one interception as UK went 7-1 in its first eight games. The Notre Dame transfer has been picked off three times, however, during the Wildcats’ current three-game losing skid. As UK played from behind in last week’s 28-14 loss at Missouri, Minchey, a 6-foot-2, 211-pound fourth-year player from Hendersonville, Tennessee, threw a season-high 43 passes, completing 27 for 288 yards with no touchdowns and two picks. • The UK defense has struggled this season against the quarterback run game and Louisville’s Lincoln Kienholz (67.5% completions, 2,739 yards, 20 touchdowns, four interceptions; 392 rushing yards, 11 touchdowns) is a more-than-capable runner. A 6-2, 215-pound junior from Pierre, South Dakota, Kienholz ran for a net-81 yards in a 44-17 win over Georgia Tech and has rushed for a net-40 yards or more in six other games. A transfer from Ohio State, Kienholz also has five games in which he has thrown for 300 yards or more, including last week’s 42-10 strafing of Pittsburgh, when he passed for 309 yards and five touchdowns vs. one interception. Advantage : Louisville Running backs • Kentucky running backs had a rough go in the loss to Missouri. UK leading rusher CJ Baxter (610 yards, 5.4 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 13 catches, 91 yards, one TD) and backup Jason Patterson (504 yards, 5.8 yards a carry, three TDs) each left the Mizzou game early due to injuries. With Baxter and Patterson sidelined, Jovantae Barnes (347 yards, 5.1 yards a carry, three TDs) carried a season-high 16 times for 69 yards at Mizzou and scored UK’s only touchdown on a 2-yard run in the fourth quarter. Barnes also lost a fourth-quarter fumble at the Missouri 13-yard line. • Louisville’s Isaac Brown (834 rushing yards, 7 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 19 catches, 177 yards, two touchdowns) missed last season’s Governor’s Cup rivalry game due to injury. As a freshman in 2024, Brown won the game’s Howard Schnellenberger MVP Award after carrying 26 times for 176 yards and two touchdowns in a 41-14 U of L rout of Kentucky at Kroger Field. Senior Keyjuan Brown (672 yards, 7 yards a carry, six TDs) has run for 50 yards or more in six straight games. Wide receivers • Kentucky freshman Kenny Darby (57 catches, 711 yards, three touchdowns) made eight receptions for a career-high 110 yards in the loss at Missouri. In so doing, the 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, moved past Barion Brown (50 receptions for 628 yards in 2022) to claim UK’s freshman record for most catches and receiving yards in a season. After missing UK’s 21-14 loss to Florida two weeks ago due to injury, senior Nic Anderson (22 catches, 242 yards, one TD) returned at Mizzou and caught two passes for 19 yards. • Louisville leading receiver Tre Richardson (58 catches, 822 yards, five touchdowns) has caught 28 passes in U of L’s past four games. A 5-10, 175-pound senior from Topeka, Kansas, Richardson had a massive game against Kentucky last season while playing for Vanderbilt. In Vandy’s 45-17 decimation of UK in Nashville, Richardson caught six passes for 159 yards and three touchdowns. TreyShun Hurry (45, 452, 3) and Lawayne McCoy (36, 640, six) are also productive. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez (58 catches, 560 yards, three touchdowns) caught eight passes for 93 yards in the loss at Missouri. That moved the 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School past Jacob Tamme (56 catches in 2007) for the most receptions in a season by a 21st Century UK tight end. Second-year player Mikkel Skinner (13, 115, 1) caught three passes for 18 yards vs. Mizzou and rushed twice for six yards. • Louisville’s Jaleel Skinner (25 catches, 362 yards, four TDs) is a cousin of UK’s Mikkel Skinner. In U of L’s 41-0 rout of Kentucky last season, Jaleel Skinner caught two passes for 21 yards and a touchdown. Advantage : Kentucky Offensive line • Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood was knocked out of the Missouri game with an injury. UK coach Will Stein said Monday that Wood’s status to play this week is “day to day.” If the ex-Madison Central standout cannot go, left guard Olaus Alinen will shift to right tackle and Jordan Knox will move into the vacated guard spot. • Louisville left tackle Lance Robinson was named Outland Trophy National Player of the Week after earning a 90 grade with three knockdown blocks in U of L’s 44-20 romp over Florida State on Oct. 9. In that game, Robinson started at right tackle, moved to left tackle and also played a series at center. Center Evan Wibberley , played last season for Kentucky after spending his first three college campaigns at Western Kentucky. Advantage : Even Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace (43 tackles, six sacks, 10.5 tackles for loss, nine quarterback hurries) tied for the team high with seven stops and had 1.5 tackles for loss at Missouri. After having a QB sack in three straight games against Oklahoma, Vanderbilt and Tennessee, Humphrey-Grace has gone the past two games without a sack. Tackle Tavion Gadson (39 tackles, three sacks, five TFL, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveries) made six tackles vs. Mizzou. • Louisville right defensive end Clev Lubin (49 tackles, nine sacks, 10 tackles for loss, seven QB hurries, two forced fumbles) is a disruptor. The 6-3, 260-pound Lubin had two sacks vs. UK last season. At right end, former UK player Jerod Smith II has made 20 tackles with 1.5 sacks and 4.5 TFL. Tackle Demeco Kennedy (28 tackles, one sack, three TFL) is a Frederick Douglass High School product who played with UK nose guard Jamarrion Harkless at both Douglass and then Purdue. • With 87 stops, Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey is the second-leading tackler in the SEC. A 6-3, 240-pound fourth-year player, Godfrey has made double-digit tackles in four games this year. SLB Sam Greene (34 tackles, 1.5 sacks, two forced fumbles, an interception) made six tackles at Mizzou. • Louisville MLB Stanquan Clark (team-high 77 tackles, 1.5 sacks, seven tackles for loss, five pass breakups, 2 QB hurries) has three double-digit tackles games this season. WLB T.J. Capers (70 tackles, 1.5 sacks, four TFL, three PBU, four QB hurries) intercepted a pass in last week’s dismantling of Pitt. Capers made four tackles, two solo, vs. UK last year. Defensive backs • The Kentucky pass defense had a rough go at Missouri, giving up 314 passing yards and four touchdown throws. Cornerback Terhyon Nichols was credited with seven tackles, broke up two passes and intercepted one. Safeties Jordan Castell and Ty Bryant each have four interceptions but Castell has gone four games and Bryant three without a pick. • Louisville strong safety Kaleb Beasley is stacking his stat line. The 6-1, 200-pound third-year player from Nashville, has made 68 tackles, broken up eight passes and intercepted five. A transfer from Tennessee, Beasley had three tackles last season for UT in the Volunteers’ 56-34 win over UK at Kroger Field. Former Kentucky defensive back DJ Waller Jr. has made 17 tackles and broken up a pass. Special teams • Kentucky place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 14 of 17 on field-goal tries with a long make of 52 yards. Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara only punted twice at Missouri, but averaged a booming 56.5 yards a kick. On the season O’Hara is averaging 42.9 yards but has pinned opponents’ inside their 20-yard line only five times on 22 kicks. Punt returner Brock Coffman , a former Louisville player, is averaging 8.9 yards on 12 returns and had a 55-yard touchdown vs. LSU. • Louisville place-kicker Carson Hilbert is 14 of 20 on field-goal tries with a long make of 54 yards. Hilbert is 6 of 12 from outside 40 yards. Punter Niall Hayes is averaging 40.2 yards and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line only nine times on 38 kicks. Punt returner Jackson Voth is averaging 13.5 yards on 14 returns with a long of 68. Isaac Brown has averaged 23.8 yards on eight kickoff returns with a long of 71. Louisville 31, Kentucky 23 Where to watch, how to follow Kentucky’s football game vs. Louisville UK’s outcome vs. U of L will dictate how many feel about Will Stein’s 1st season Kentucky football’s Will Stein supports a 24-team CFP. home.blurb: “So he’ll do some halfcourt stuff and individual stuff,” Underwood said of Mirkovic. “So they’ve got it all mapped out. The progression, and what he does on the treadmills, what he does on the pools, what he does on the court before he’s live. Illinois basketball carries a 6-1 record into Thanksgiving, despite having been without star forward David Mirkovic in every game thus far. Freshman phenom Quentin Coleman and veteran wing Andrej Stojakovic have carried the load, while a handful of other freshmen have made an unexpected impact. The Illini see one more mid-major squad – Western Kentucky – before their date with UConn in Chicago , which will be followed by a pair of Big Ten games. But Friday's contest against the Hilltoppers is hardly a freebie. Illinois coach Brad Underwood explains: Illinois' Brad Underwood previews Western Kentucky “[We] get a very, very hard-playing, very, very athletic, very, very good defensive team in Western Kentucky coming in here,” Underwood said. “I think if you look at KenPom, they maybe have one loss scheduled after this game on paper. This is a very, very good basketball team." It's important to note that Underwood characterizes every Illini opponent with some version of "a very good basketball team." But this time around, it isn't just hyperbole. Western Kentucky ranks No. 99 in KenPom. That’s 10 spots above Northwestern and just two spots behind Penn State. And defense – specifically the ability to create chaos on that end – is indeed the Hilltoppers’ calling card, as Underwood emphasized throughout his review. WKU is No. 15 in the country in turnovers forced – an area that has been one of Illinois’ few offensive vulnerabilities – at 18.43 per game. “Extremely athletic, physical,” Underwood said. “They’re very good at what they do defensively. Little guard – [Sharron] Young – is one of the tops in steals in the country. They force a ton of [turnovers]. They’ve had a 23-point lead at Tulsa. They’ve got the [Teagan] Moore kid – is the best player in Conference USA. He reminds me a lot of Marcus Domask in terms of physicality. Can handle it. Can shoot it. Scores in a lot of ways. But this team is driven by their defense. Hank [Plona] does a great job on that end. “You can’t give them live-ball pick sizes. You’ve got to protect it. A lot of switching. It’ll be very similar to some Nebraska-type defensive rotations, and a lot of switching. They’ll press us some. They’ll play some zone. home.blurb: Wildcats fans are hopeful Moreno will be available for Friday’s game against Wichita State, but his long-term health remains the priority as the season continues. With Moreno’s status still uncertain, Kentucky will need its other frontcourt players to step up if the sophomore center is unable to return against Wichita State. Kentucky basketball has stumbled out of the gate. Here’s a look at the Wildcats’ best-case scenario, worst-case scenario, and updated season prediction. For Kentucky Basketball , it feels like when it rains, it pours, and the struggles continue to pile up for the Wildcats. Kentucky has struggled against weaker opponents; along with that, it has suffered blowout losses against some of the better teams on its schedule. Now, the Wildcats could be without one of their most important players as they look to get the season back on track. On Sunday, Matt Jones of Kentucky Sports Radio reported that sophomore center Malachi Moreno had entered concussion protocol after an Indiana player dove on him during Kentucky’s loss to the Hoosiers. Moreno hit his head on the floor during the play and was unlikely to play in Friday’s matchup against Wichita State. Although Moreno remained in the game against Indiana, head coach Mark Pope provided an update on the sophomore big man during his radio show on Tuesday, explaining that Moreno began experiencing concussion symptoms on Saturday. “He’s doing good,” Pope said on his radio show. “He kind of got a whole 270 pounds landed on his head, and kind of started after the game, and then especially, really the next day, started showing some symptoms. “So we put him in concussion protocol, and he’s responded really, really well, and so we’re hopeful that he’ll be back sooner rather than later because he’s playing so well.” For Kentucky, losing Moreno for multiple games would be a significant setback, especially considering how productive he has been this season. The sophomore center is averaging 13.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.8 blocks, and 1.2 steals in 27.8 minutes per game. “He’s put up huge numbers, and he’s just playing at such a high level,” Pope continued. “It’s really important for us to get him back. We can’t wait till we get him back, and he’ll continue on with the terrific season.” All of your communities in one place. This is the title for the native ad More in Kentucky Wildcats Basketball

picks.headline: Five final thoughts, score prediction for South Carolina football vs. Clemson
picks.blurb: Five final thoughts, score prediction for South Carolina football vs. Clemson - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games NBA Cup: Knockouts set Friday's college football scores Steelers dominate without Rodgers Luka shoved by fan USWNT qualifies for 2027 World Cup Five final thoughts, score prediction for South Carolina football vs. Clemson South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer and his son Hunter speak with Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney on the field before the Palmetto Bowl between at Memorial Stadium in Clemson on Saturday, November 30, 2024. (Sam Wolfe/Special To The State) Jordan Kaye · The State Fri, November 27, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After finishing its SEC schedule with back-to-back losses to Arkansas and No. 1 Georgia, South Carolina (6-5) concludes the regular-season Saturday afternoon at Clemson (7-4). This will be the 123rd meeting between the Gamecocks and Tigers. Clemson leads the all-time series 74-44-4 and holds bragging rights after getting the 28-14 win over USC last year in Williams-Brice Stadium. The game is set to kick off at 3 p.m. and will be broadcast on ESPN2. And the betting public continues to back South Carolina. After opening as field-goal favorites, the Gamecocks are currently favored by 6 points. Those are some facts. Here are some thoughts. 1. South Carolina can't lose this game You'd quicker find a South Carolina fan who puts Will Muschamp on their Mount Rushmore than one who finds it acceptable losing to Clemson. But, certainly, during the late 2010s, when the Tigers were competing for national titles, it was a stretch to expect a Gamecock win. This year has been different. Ever since LSU used Clemson as its Week-1 cupcake, rolling to a 41-point win, South Carolina fans began salivating over the thought of a Spurrier-esque whooping on Nov. 28. This is the worst Clemson team in at least 16 years, and there's no reason the Gamecocks shouldn't take full advantage. That sentiment has changed a bit over the past few weeks as the Gamecocks have scored a combined 12 points against Arkansas and Georgia while Clemson looked competent in last week's win over Duke, sparked by the play of third-string quarterback Trent Pearman. Pearman has all the makings of a rivalry hero. He's the son of former Clemson assistant Danny Pearman, grew up around the Carolina-Clemson rivalry and will likely play the last two football games of his life before taking a normal-person job. He's the type of guy announcers gush over for hours as they show baby pictures of him in Clemson gear and tell us 15 times how it's "in his blood." "I can work a 9 to 5 the rest of my life," Pearman said this week. "This week is all about Clemson-South Carolina." It's up to the Gamecocks to make Saturday a nightmare for Pearman, to make it clear to every person watching why he was the Tigers' third-string option who's only playing because the other two got hurt. It's hard to imagine the embarrassment for South Carolina if it lost to this Clemson team, and the offseason ramifications that would ensure. No, not Shane Beamer getting fired . That's not happening, regardless of the result. But no staff change could be ruled out. No recruiting flip would be off the table. Nothing would be secure. That would make for a miserable offseason filled and real doubt about the future of the program. A win salvages optimism, especially if it's followed by a bowl victory. Folks in Columbia won't be — and shouldn't be — satisfied with eight wins, but it would be something to rally behind as the Gamecocks push to make the 24-team playoff next year. 2. LaNorris Sellers' decision looms After talking with three sources who would have knowledge of the situation, there is consensus that LaNorris Sellers has not made a decision about his plans for the 2027 season yet. Perhaps that's to be expected. He can sit down after the season and get a better feel for where he'd be projected to go in the NFL Draft if he wanted to declare. If we consider the reports that Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor is reportedly getting $7.5 million to return to Starkville next year and assume a Sellers contract would be in the same ballpark, it would be financially wise for him to return to college ... unless he's for sure going to be a first-round NFL Draft pick. Coming back would also give him another chance to play with his brother, USC receiver Jayden Sellers, who missed all season with an injury. And, well, many NFL Draft insiders have noted that Sellers would benefit from another year in college, especially if he can work with OC Kendal Briles again. Remember, the Gamecocks have had three different offensive coordinators in Sellers' three seasons as a starter. "LaNorris Sellers, there is a strong opinion in NFL scouting circles … that he will be back in school next year," draft analyst Todd McShay , who spent 17 years working at ESPN, said on his podcast in November. "That he absolutely needs to for his development." While Sellers' put together a monstrous highlight montage during the Gamecocks' four-game winning streak this season — remembered most by touchdown runs against Tennessee and Texas A&M — he was wildly inconsistent during the first month of the season and has been dealing with an ankle injury for much of the last three weeks. One can only imagine what Beamer would give for Sellers to return. Everything becomes so much easier if No. 16 comes back. Retaining Briles, whose name has been mentioned for the TCU head coaching job. Keeping your signing class intact. Attracting transfers. Talking with boosters. Garnering excitement about 2027. Hope becomes easy. Lose Sellers and, boy, the Gamecocks are in for a stressful offseason. 3. Home woes are bizarre The home team has not won the Palmetto Bowl since 2018, a stat that becomes harder to fathom as it continues to grow. While Carolina and Clemson didn't play in 2020, the road team has won the last six matchups in this rivalry. How rare is that? Well, we looked through the history of every SEC's teams rivalries (Alabama-Auburn, Florida-Florida State, etc.) and couldn't find another instance of six-straight road rivalry wins. The only time another rivalry has even come close in the last 80-plus years was Georgia-Georgia Tech about a decade ago. From 2013 to 2017 (five matchups), the road team was victorious in "Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate." "I think that's really, really hard to (win on the road) in a rivalry game," Beamer said, "so it's really fascinating to me that the road team has been able to do it so many consecutive games." The Carolina-Clemson road streak will be broken eventually. The Gamecocks hope it's not until next year. 4. Don't let this game come down to a kick While South Carolina's sophomore kicker Malik Orsan — a Southeast Missouri State transfer who enrolled this summer — has been solid as a first-year starter, hitting 13 of 17 field-goal attempts (including two from beyond 50), he will not be the best leg on Saturday. Clemson junior Nolan Hauser is arguably the best kicker in America, a Lou Groza Award finalist who tied the single-season NCAA record last week with his 31st made kick. He is 31 for 34 this season, including 15 of 18 from beyond 40 yards. South Carolina has to ensure this game is not close enough to be decided by kickers. 5. The playoff isn't a guarantee There are some college football plans who hear the words "24-team playoff" and think every team in the SEC is going to earn a bid. Heck, every SEC fan base is going to expect to be in that playoff come 2027. But, as this Gamecocks' season proved, it's not that easy. South Carolina would not have made the 24-team playoff this year. The Gamecocks have only been inside the Top 25 of the College Football Playoff Rankings on selection day three times in the last decade, and only twice under Beamer (2022 and 2024). Yes, Gamecock fans will rightfully rejoice if/when South Carolina makes the playoff. But the sting of the previous season is going to be that much worse if it's on the outside looking in. PREDICTION: South Carolina 20, Clemson 16

Clemson is now 7-4 on the season, with the team having won four of its last six games overall. The Tigers have rebounded nicely from a poor opening part of the season, despite a lackluster offense all year. But as the Tigers prepare for the final week of the regular season, the only focus is on getting a win over the rival South Carolina Gamecocks. Clemson will be hosting South Carolina in the game, giving themselves a slight edge entering the contest. South Carolina will come into the game with a record of 6-5 for the season, coming off two straight blow out losses. The Gamecocks have lost by a score of 34-6 in two straight weeks, and they will try to bounce back this week against Clemson. Both sides understand the rivalry aspect of this game, with the Tigers wanting to add another win to the season's resume. But South Carolina won't go down quietly, looking to spoil the Tigers' final home game of the year. Heading into the game, the Tigers are being viewed as the underdogs, despite having the better record than South Carolina. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Clemson has a 44.2 percent chance of taking down the Gamecocks this week at home. Quarterback Trent Pearman will likely get the starting nod in this game after leading the Tigers to a win last week. Pearman did well enough for Clemson to win, and it seems that the program wants to see more from him in this game. Overall, Pearman went 17-of-27 for 164 yards, with no touchdown passes against the Blue Devils. But he did rush for 51 yards and a touchdown, showing that he can be a dual-threat option for Clemson. If Pearman can continue to help the offense, it could give Clemson an opportunity to grab the win. Clemson's defense has been strong all year, and South Carolina's offense has been very stagnant over the last few weeks. Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney has been criticized all season long , but if this team could get a win over the Gamecocks, it could go a long way for him. The 2026 season won't be seen as a complete success, but after how it started, the Tigers may end the year on a high note.

The former Clemson offensive lineman expects the Tigers to close the regular season with a second straight upset after winning 20-10 at Duke last Friday. "With all that said, Clemson is about to whip that ass," Mac Lain said. "I cannot wait to see this. The Tigers are going to win this thing." The former Clemson football player came down with a late third-quarter interception against rivals South Carolina on Saturday night, ending a Gamecocks red-zone threat and helping top-ranked Georgia hold a 27-6 lead going into the fourth quarter. South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers was driving inside the Georgia 22 when he forced a throw into traffic. Barnes was lingering and waiting. The pick took away South Carolina's best chance to cut into the deficit and handed the ball straight back to the Bulldogs. It was the only turnover of the night for either team at that point and the only one South Carolina couldn't afford at the time. The Gamecocks, ranked 21st at 6-4, had managed just two field goals before the interception. Georgia, 9-1 and ranked first, had already built a two-score cushion behind two Nate Frazier rushing touchdowns and a pair of field goals from Peyton Woodring. For Clemson fans, the sight of Barnes snuffing out a South Carolina drive had to feel familiar probably even a tad bit confusing for the head to digest. He left Death Valley, but nobody let his instincts know that they should do the same. Somewhere in Upstate South Carolina, Tigers fans are watching a former player in a Bulldogs jersey do exactly what they would have asked of him, and deciding whether to be proud or just slightly annoyed that it's happening in another uniform. Barnes may be wearing a Georgia G now, but the Tiger paw is clearly still stamped somewhere in his blood. The Gamecocks will need to regroup quickly if they are to win this one. away.headline: Dabo Swinney Drops Sobering Injury Update Ahead of South Carolina Showdown
away.blurb: Clemson emerged from Friday night’s 20-10 road victory over Duke largely unscathed, though veteran quarterback Christopher Vizzina remains ruled out ahead of Saturday’s regular-season finale against rival South Carolina at Memorial Stadium. “ Injury wise, we came through it pretty good, so that was a positive,” Swinney said. “Hopefully everybody that played in the game will be able to keep going and finish this thing up strong. Nothing coming out of the game that was too worrisome, and then hopefully w e’ll get a couple guys back as well.” While Swinney is hopeful that everyone who suited up against Duke will be available—and that a few injured players could return—Vizzina will not be among them. The veteran signal-caller continues to recover from a severe concussion sustained late in Clemson’s 20-6 loss to Georgia Tech. With Vizzina sidelined and Tait Reynolds already out for the season following knee surgery, Clemson has turned to fifth-year senior Trent Pearman, who led the Tigers (7-4) past Duke in his first career start. Dabo Swinney Drops Sobering Injury Update Ahead of South Carolina Showdown Unlock the latest Heavy on Clemson news — direct to your inbox. During his Sunday evening teleconference, Tigers head coach Dabo Swinney offered an encouraging assessment of his roster’s overall health following the win over the Blue Devils. “Oh, no, no, no, he’s nowhere near being back,” Swinney said. “I don’t think people realize how severe that was. He definitely will not be back.” Vizzina was taken to a hospital for precautionary evaluations after suffering the injury against Georgia Tech. Although tests on his neck and spine came back clear, significant concussion symptoms have persisted, capping an injury-marred 2026 campaign that has also included a broken arm and an ankle injury. “Again, it just breaks my heart for him,” Swinney said. “He was healthy for one game and two series of the second game, and outside of that, he’s … between the broken arm, the ankle, and now the concussion, it’s been a tough year.” The severity of his symptoms prevented Vizzina from participating in team activities last week, though Swinney hopes the quarterback can rejoin his teammates off the field during game week. “He couldn’t really even be around last week with the symptoms he was dealing with,” Swinney said. “Hopefully he’ll be able to be back and be in meetings and stuff this week, and finish up with these guys.” Saturday’s rivalry matchup against South Carolina is scheduled for a 3 p.m. kickoff on ESPN2. Clemson, which has lost its last two home games against the Gamecocks, enters the contest as a 4.5-point underdog according to FanDuel Sportsbook. Wide receiver Tyler Brown has missed three straight games with an ankle injury, and his status for South Carolina seems up in the air. Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney briefly discussed Brown during his weekly radio show on Monday, and he didn't seem to have much of an update. All Swinney had to say was that Brown was "still working his way back, so we'll see." That doesn't exactly sound too promising. Brown has caught 36 passes for 332 yards in eight games this season, representing a solid bounce-back year for the senior playmaker who was largely invisible two campaigns in a row for the Tigers. Brown arrived at Clemson in 2023 and actually got off to a terrific start, hauling in 52 receptions for 531 yards and four touchdowns. It has been a rough go for the 21-year-old ever since. Then, last year, Brown managed just 22 grabs for 191 yards. Brown has not reached the end zone since his debut campaign, and while that has a whole lot to do with him falling behind T.J. Moore and Bryant Wesco on the depth chart, it's fair to say that more was expected from him after his initial showing. He certainly appeared to be on a positive trajectory this season, but the ankle injury he sustained a few weeks ago has certainly thrown a wrench into things. Clemson was able to win without Brown last Friday, coming through with a surprising 20-10 victory over the Duke Blue Devils on the road. Moore led the way with four catches for 68 yards in the win. Wesco added two receptions for 12 yards. The Tigers improved to 7-4 with the victory, but they'll be facing a south Gamecocks squad with a dangerous offense this weekend. Luckily for the Tigers, their defense has been phenomenal this season, so hopefully Clemson can hold LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina offense in check. We'll see if any positive developments occur for Brown during the week.

Fortunately, the USC offense got gritty with the run game, taking pressure off quarterback Jayden Maiava while providing an easy check-down option and milking the clock. The dynamic duo of Waymond Jordan and King Miller accounted for 140 of USC’s 184 rushing yards. Jordan – 18 carries, 70 yards, two touchdowns – looks healthy as ever, with his quick cuts and strong finishes. Miller – 10 carries for 70 yards – continues to shine as the explosive runner and is a huge plus as an easy pass option. It's also worth noting that Southern Cal is 8-1 when they rush for 100-plus yards and 0-2 when they rush for less than 100 – both of which were on the road. Riley has seemed to grow fond of the 12-personnel look and two-back backfield, which only opens up the passing game when the backfield duo is rolling. He needs to lean on it once again. Going against the Bruins' defense won't be an easy task, as the unit is No. 6 in rushing yards allowed per game (88.5) and No. 4 in yards per rush (2.7), but if USC can sustain drives with the run, they can tire out and punish this defense. With Miller as the lead rusher this time around, the two will combine for 120-plus yards and account for two scores on the day. 3. Double Digit Victory for the USC Trojans USC has won by double digits five times this season. While all five were at home, the Trojans won’t be dealing with the away-game narrative at the Rose Bowl. Similar to the Ohio State game, the defense will keep everything in front of them while flustering a young, backup quarterback. The offense will be willing to play a smash-mouth game while getting the ball to wideout Trent Mosley for explosive plays for a final score of 35-17. But if Chesney avoids going with two passers, look for true freshman Madden Iamaleava to handle the reins for UCLA. USC vs UCLA is a big deal because … 1) It's a battle between two top-15 teams in the latest College Football Playoff rankings. 2) A loss for USC would be devastating and could lead to a whole lot of changes, because … 3) UCLA is No. 9 with a 10-1 record, winning this game might be the only thing that gives the Big Ten a chance at getting two teams into the CFP. 4) It's USC vs UCLA. It might not be Ohio State-Michigan or Auburn-Alabama, but it's a big deal made bigger by the emergence of the Bruins. Back to the key part of all that. If UCLA wins, it's in the Big Ten Championship. Even if it loses, it can get in if Nebraska beats Iowa, Indiana gets by Purdue, and Washington beats Oregon – but it gets messier than that. Get past all the implications. It's a big showdown, the optics on a November afternoon in LA will be gorgeous, and it should be a blast. USC vs UCLA: Quick Hits USC has alternated win-loss over the last four games, losing to Wisconsin and Indiana on the road, and beating Ohio State and Maryland at home. UCLA suffered its first loss of the season at Michigan last week. This is the second time it has started a season 10-1 since 1998. USC has won three of the last four in the series. UCLA hasn't won at home against the Trojans since 2018. How To Watch USC vs UCLA Date: Saturday, November 28, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: CBS Location: Rose Bowl, Pasadena, CA – Week 13 Schedule, Game Previews – CFP and Bowl Projections Why USC Will Win Madden Iamalaeava. The younger brother of injured starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava doesn't have the experience, and it showed in the overtime loss against Michigan. The skills are good, and the potential is great, but how much will the Bruins hide their third-string guy? It's not like Ty Dieffenbach is Joe Burrow, but he was a solid replacement for Nico over the last six weeks, hitting the midrange throws needed to keep the train running. (Quick note: Dieffenbach isn't ruled out for this after suffering a hip injury late against Michigan, but for now, just assume it's Madden Iamalaeava.) The USC run defense has been solid – that's not the issue. The Trojans have a bigger problem with sharp passing games. UCLA won't have that. Why UCLA Will Win Grind it, play great defense, work the clock, get to Jayden Maiava before he can get comfortable, and hope it all works out. Of course, the pressure isn't off – just the opposite – but the quarterback situation means the team has to hyperfocus on what it does well. The Bruins are No. 1 in the nation at coming up with takeaways, fifth in the country at controlling the clock, and third in total defense. This has to be a field position game that puts Iamaleava in situations where he can take off when he has the chance. This will be a conservative UCLA game plan, but … USC vs UCLA Prediction, Betting Lines UCLA won't play scared. The Bruins will attack, with a run defense that takes a page out of Wisconsin's playbook. The Badgers stuffed the Trojans for -18 rushing yards, and while UCLA won't do that, it'll hold its own on the line. UCLA lost last week because the Michigan defense is the real deal. It was able to stuff everything the Bruin ground game tried to do, mainly because it's just that good up front. USC will get up early, but Wayne Knight and the Bruin ground game will start to take over in the fourth quarter. It'll come down to turnovers and field goals, and UCLA will win in both areas. away.blurb: On Wednesday, UCLA officially listed Dieffenbach as questionable on its initial Big Ten availability report ahead of Saturday's rivalry game against the USC Trojans. While the designation doesn't guarantee Dieffenbach will play, the quarterback hasn't been ruled out just days after suffering the injury. CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reported Monday that Dieffenbach's injury wasn't considered long-term. ESPN's Pete Thamel went further, reporting the quarterback could return as soon as Saturday to face the Trojans. Dieffenbach suffered hip and leg injuries at the start of the first overtime. He left the field on a stretcher , and a medical cart got him to the locker room at Ann Arbor. UCLA head coach Bob Chesney shared an encouraging update on Dieffenbach's condition earlier this week, as the quarterback participated in the Bruins' practices. UCLA has prepared backup Madden Iamaleava to potentially make his first career start this weekend, with Chesney confirming the quarterback received first-team reps to start the week. UCLA enters Saturday's matchup ranked No. 9 in the CFP standings with a 10-1 record, including a 7-1 mark in Big Ten play. A victory over No. 15 USC at the Rose Bowl would secure the Bruins a place in the Big Ten Championship Game. home.headline: UCLA's Ty Dieffenbach is latest example of confusing injury reports
home.blurb: On Monday, the national reporting on the health status of UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach contained multiple contradictions. ESPN's Pete Thamel, for instance, wrote in a tweet that "Ty Dieffenbach isn't expected to be out long-term. While his status is uncertain for this week against USC, Dieffenbach is dealing with a minor hip injury. Dieffenbach is expected to be available for the College Football Playoff should UCLA clinch a bid." That piece of reporting veers in several different directions. When a player "isn't expected to be out long-term," that is generally viewed as news that an injury will be weeks instead of months or the full season. That does mean, however, that the injury carries short-term costs. If an injury isn't "long-term," it is short-term, so it exists. If an injury isn't short-term (meaning that the player is healthy enough to play his next game), there's no point or purpose in even saying whether the injury is long-term. Notice also how the reportage focuses on Ty Dieffenbach could be ready for the College Football Playoff in mid-December but also contains that oh-by-the-way part about maybe playing this week. All of this feels like a misdirection play, and it's understandable why UCLA might not be telling the exact truth. The Bruins have no incentive to do so, calling to mind the Florida State situation in 2023, when the Seminoles were left out of the playoff due to the injury to quarterback Jordan Travis. All of this aside, however, injury reports have become a source of confusion before this Dieffenbach situation at UCLA. USC football has featured plenty of situations in the Lincoln Riley era in which a player was abruptly announced as being out of a game when there were no outward indications of an injury absence during the week. Other players have been reported as having a chance to return on a given weekend only to miss that game and then multiple games after that, which meant that the original possibility of playing in Week X was never realistic. TV, kickoff details End of the line, where we'll see two old foes meet for the 99th time. Missouri football hosts Oklahoma this coming Saturday, Nov. 28, for its regular season finale in Columbia. The Tigers are currently ranked No. 23 in the top 25 of the College Football Playoff rankings, and the Sooners are No. 17. The last game between these two teams on Faurot Field was a thriller. Mizzou scored 14 points in the final 63 seconds of the game to win the first reunion between the former Big Eight and Big 12 rivals. The Tigers (7-4, 4-4 SEC) are playing for a fourth straight season with eight or more regular season wins and a winning record in SEC play. Should MU beat the Sooners, Eli Drinkwitz's contract also will automatically be extended by one year. Oklahoma (7-4, 5-3) has won its last three games to right the ship on its season. The Sooners effectively shut Missouri's offense down in a 17-6 win last season in Norman. These teams, who first faced off in 1902, are playing for the 99th time Saturday. Here's what you need to know about Oklahoma before Saturday's regular-season finale: Oklahoma has committed to running struggling QB John Mateer Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer (10) runs with the ball during his team's 2025 game against Missouri at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. The Sooners have gotten out of their offensive rut by committing to running quarterback John Mateer, who was really struggling to begin this season. At the start of November, the Sooners fired offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle and replaced him with interim play caller Jason Witten. The major change the Sooners have made is getting their quarterback going with his legs, and that's led to an uptick in overall production and fewer turnovers — a good combination. Mateer was averaging nine carries per game for 32 rushing yards per game. Since the OC change, he's taken an average of 13.3 carries for 71.3 yards on the ground per game. OU has averaged 161.3 yards of rushing offense per game in wins over Florida, Ole Miss and Texas A&M in November. The Sooners had only surpassed 161.3 rushing yards in two of their previous eight games. Mateer threw seven interceptions in the opening eight games of the year and fumbled five times. He's thrown one pick and had one fumble in the last three games. More: Missouri faces Oklahoma offense that's found new life in November What makes the OU defense consistently excellent? Brent Venables: Defensive play-caller in name only. "He's got a stylistic way that he calls defenses that he almost approaches it, to me, like an offensive coordinator does. He's not very defensive," MU coach Eli Drinkwitz said. "He's pretty offensive as a defensive coordinator, where he is setting the tone and taking the fight to you." Oklahoma, as tends to be the case, ranks among the better statistical defenses in the SEC this season. The Sooners rank fourth in the conference by allowing 284.6 yards of offense per game, including the best pass defense at 163.1 yards per game. The Sooners are on track to field a top-20 defense in FBS for total yards allowed per game for a third straight season — every year since joining the SEC. "I was speaking with somebody and they said the top 14 players on the Oklahoma defense all have played their entire career at Oklahoma and have been there the whole time," Drinkwitz said, "which gives you a foundation so that when you're walking through or showing this defense and you use terms like 'this is how we played it last year, this is what we did last time,' or they've seen that install, there's the repetition. There's the foundation of what they're going to do." Who are OU's top playmakers? Drinkwitz said Oklahoma has the "best defensive front that we've seen all year." The Sooners have nine different players with at least 3.5 tackles for loss this season. Eight different players have registered multiple sacks. Defensive tackle David Stone, who has 4.5 sacks from the interior, and experienced linebacker Owen Heinecke, who has 11.5 tackles for loss, are likely All-SEC picks. Most of Oklahoma's receiving production has come via two players: wide receiver Isaiah Sategna and tight end Rocky Beers. Sategna has caught 56 passes for 722 yards and five touchdowns, and he has also returned two punts for touchdowns this year. Beers has 49 catches for 626 receiving yards and five touchdowns, which leads SEC tight ends. Score prediction: Missouri 17, Oklahoma 14 More: Naeshaun Montgomery spent nights in the Mizzou locker room. No one's sleeping on him now. Oklahoma is as strong as always on the defensive side of the ball and has found something it can lean on with its offense. This has the makings of a game that comes down to the wire (and one that maybe looks a little ugly along the way). We'll give the Tigers the edge on their home field. Broadcast Details - TV: SEC Network and ESPN Unlimited (Dave Neal, Cole Cubelic and Tori Petry) - Radio: Sooner Sports Network via 107.7 The Franchise/KOKC 95.3 and 1520 in Oklahoma City, 1430 The Buzz/KMOD 97.5 in Tulsa, and on The Varsity Network app (Toby Rowland, Teddy Lehman, Chris Plank, and Gabe Ikard) What You Need To Know COLUMBIA, Mo. — Oklahoma (7-4, 5-3 SEC) will look to extend their win streak to four as they head to Faurot Field to take on Missouri (7-4, 4-4 SEC). The Sooners have strung together three straight wins over Florida, Ole Miss, and Texas A&M after alternating wins and losses in each of their first nine games this year, the longest such streak in program history to open a season. The Sooners' 10th opponent out of 12 this fall will be the Missouri Tigers, who were either ranked or receiving votes in at least one major poll at kickoff. Only Oklahoma's opener against UTEP and last week's opponent, Texas A&M, were not ranked or receiving votes. This will be the 99th meeting between the two former conference rivals . The series is 68-25-5 in Oklahoma's favor, including a 9-2 record in the last 11 meetings, 21-3 in the last 24 meetings, and 23-7 in the last 30 meetings in Columbia. OU is 17-6 all-time against ranked Missouri teams. The Sooners and Tigers have played each other as members of the Missouri Valley Intercollegiate Athletic Association, the Big Seven, the Big Eight, the Big 12, and now in the SEC. Under Sooners head coach Brent Venables , OU is 1-1 against Missouri. The Tigers got the best of Oklahoma in their first meeting as SEC institutions in 2024, with a 30-23 win in Columbia. Then in 2025, Oklahoma returned the favor with a 17-6 victory in Norman. Since last season, OU has won five of its last six SEC road games (excluding a 27-24 win over No. 1 Texas in Dallas in 2024), including wins at Mississippi State and No. 25 Florida in 2026 and wins at South Carolina, No. 14 Tennessee, and No. 4 Alabama in 2025. Oklahoma's offense has found new life this month since Jason Witten was promoted from tight ends coach to interim offensive coordinator. Under Witten, the Sooners have averaged 25 points per game. OU's offense has done a much better job of playing complementary football, controlling the clock, running the football, and making life easier on the defense by keeping them off the field. As a result, the Sooners' defense has allowed an average of just 10 points per game over their last three contests. With only five drives of 10 or more plays in the first five games of the season, Oklahoma has had 18 such drives in the last six games. This includes a 20-play, 12:45 drive for a touchdown against Florida, the Sooners' longest such drive since 1972 and the longest by any SEC team this season. Third-down conversions have improved from 37% in the first eight games to 52% under Witten, and time of possession is averaging 36:08 per game (fifth in the country and best among Power Four teams during the stretch). Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer has played better in the Sooners' last three games than in the previous nine, scoring three touchdowns on 335 total yards in last week's 28-7 win over Texas A&M and three touchdowns on 337 total yards in the previous three games. His three highest rushing totals of the season have come in those last three games (56 yards at Florida, 70 vs. Ole Miss, 66 vs. Texas A&M). He has rushed for 192 of his 337 rushing yards in the three games Witten has called the plays. This includes both of his rushing touchdowns this season, running behind the same five offensive linemen in each of those three games: Michael Fasusi, Noah Best, Jake Maikkula, Heath Ozaeta, and E'Marion Harris. Isaiah Sategna III leads the Sooners in receiving with 56 catches for 722 yards and five touchdowns, averaging 102.3 all-purpose yards per game, including two punt-return touchdowns. Mackey Award semifinalist Rocky Beers is averaging 56.9 yards receiving per game, most in the SEC among tight ends, with five touchdowns, most by an OU tight end since Mark Andrews in 2017. Lloyd Avant, Tory Blaylock and Jonathan Hatton Jr. are contributing on the ground for the Sooners. Missouri (5-1 at home, 2-3 on the road) started the season 5-1 and rose to No. 13 in the AP poll before losing three of their last five games. However, they most recently pulled off a 28-14 win against No. 16 Kentucky. The Tigers can rely on left-handed quarterback Austin Simmons . This season, Simmons has thrown for 2,693 yards, 25 touchdowns, and four interceptions. Mizzou's backfield is loaded with 1,200-yard rusher Jamal Roberts and 2025 All-American Ahmad Hardy, who is returning from a leg injury. The Tigers' offense also includes dynamic receivers in Cayden Lee and Donovan Olugbode. Missouri has had a great season defensively, leading the SEC in turnover margin. However, the Tigers allow a lot of passing yards and have given up quite a few explosive plays this season. That means Mateer and Witten can get things done on offense if Oklahoma can protect the football as they have in the last five games, with just two total giveaways. The Sooners' defense is made up of all homegrown players who started their college careers in Norman. All 15 players who have started at least one game this season play on defense. Oklahoma's defense is top-20 in the country in third-down defense (27.4%, No. 3), first downs allowed (14.3 per game, No. 3), passing defense (163.1 ypg, No. 7), red-zone defense (72.0%, No. 8), total defense (284.6 ypg, No. 12), sacks (2.8 per game, No. 17), and scoring defense (17.9 ppg, No. 18). With Butkus Award semifinalist Owen Heinecke leading the Sooners' defense in tackles with 91, 11.5 for loss, as well as Kip Lewis, David Stone, and lockdown corner Courtland Guillory (36.2 passer rating allowed when targeted), Oklahoma will be looking to have a clean, tackling-focused, disciplined game in Columbia on Saturday.

picks.headline: Week 13 college football betting, odds: 3 early bets to make right now, including in Oklahoma-Missouri
picks.blurb: Week 13 college football betting, odds: 3 early bets to make right now, including in Oklahoma-Missouri - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games NBA Cup: Knockouts set Friday's college football scores Steelers dominate without Rodgers Luka shoved by fan USWNT qualifies for 2027 World Cup Corbie Craig Contributing writer Tue, November 24, 2026 at 10:55 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads College football rivalry week is here, and some of the toughest teams to price are the ones making changes this late in the season. Oklahoma has won three straight with Jason Witten calling plays, Minnesota just won after changing its offensive coordinator, and Wisconsin got a big performance from a quarterback who had lost his starting job. There are reasons to believe those offenses are improving, but I want to be careful about how much of last Saturday carries into this week. I'm starting with three unders, looking at the way these teams have been moving the ball and how much work it takes them to score. Here are my three early Week 13 bets. No. 19 Oklahoma at No. 24 Missouri (-1.5, 41.5) Oklahoma has looked better since Witten took over. Quarterback John Mateer has settled down, and the offense is giving its defense a chance to rest. I understand why people would expect more points here. Against Ole Miss, all three of Oklahoma's offensive scoring drives took at least 12 plays, and Isaiah Sategna added a punt-return touchdown, which helped turn a game in which Mateer threw for 111 yards into a 24-17 win. Then against Texas A&M, the Sooners were tied entering the fourth quarter before finishing a 15-play touchdown drive that took more than eight minutes. A later interception set up a one-play touchdown to Sategna, making the final score look a lot more comfortable than the game had been. Witten can keep Mateer in manageable situations, use the running game and keep Missouri's offense off the field. Oklahoma's defense has held Florida and Texas A&M to seven points apiece during this stretch, with Ole Miss scoring 17 between them. Missouri will test it. QB Austin Simmons threw four touchdown passes against Kentucky, and WR Donovan Olugbode caught two of them. I'm more concerned about those receivers creating quick scores than Missouri consistently driving the length of the field. The Tigers also allowed Kentucky into the red zone seven times while giving up only 14 points, so their defense gave up more chances than the final score suggests. I expect Oklahoma to stick with the patient approach that has worked under Witten, while making Simmons put together longer drives to score. Bet: Under 41.5 (-110) Minnesota at Wisconsin (-7.5, 37.5) Wisconsin just scored 42 points at Purdue, so this is a pretty low number to come back and bet under. RB Colton Joseph returned to the starting job and ran for 187 yards, including touchdowns from 32 and 66 yards out. Darrion Dupree broke a long touchdown run, too. Purdue couldn't handle the quarterback run game, and Wisconsin kept going back to it. Minnesota has to do a better job there. The Gophers allowed Northwestern to rush for 196 yards, and Joseph gave Wisconsin a way to turn a missed assignment into a touchdown without throwing the ball. That's the biggest concern with this bet — but I still don't trust Minnesota to score much. P.J. Fleck fired offensive coordinator Greg Harbaugh Jr. after the Penn State loss, and Eric Koehler took over the play-calling against Northwestern. Darius Taylor ran the ball better and two missed field goals hurt, but the Gophers still went into halftime scoreless. Their first touchdown required a fourth-down conversion, and Anthony Smith then forced and recovered a fumble to give Minnesota a short field for its second TD. QB Drake Lindsey made a great throw late to set up the winning field goal, but even with those plays, Minnesota finished with only 20 points. It hasn't scored more than that in any of its past six games. I can give the coaching change some credit without expecting everything to be fixed before a trip to Wisconsin. The Badgers' defense ranks No. 21 in our ratings, and neither offense is in much of a hurry between snaps. If Minnesota can make Joseph and Dupree string together first downs instead of breaking long runs, Wisconsin can move the ball while taking plenty of time off the clock. Bet: Under 37.5 (-110) North Dakota State (-9.5, 39.5) at San José State San José State nearly forced overtime against UNLV, but the offense still had to work awfully hard to get to 22 points. QB Luke Weaver threw 40 passes while the Spartans ran for just 56 yards. They needed a late touchdown pass to Carson Clark to get within a 2-point conversion then couldn't complete the tying attempt. A week earlier, they scored three points at Air Force. We still rank this offense 128th, and I'm not convinced Weaver gets enough help from the running game to keep it moving against North Dakota State. The Bison's defense certainly gave us a reason to hesitate last week. They led Northern Illinois 31-3 before allowing touchdowns on the Huskies' final three possessions. I still put more weight on a defense we rank No. 29, which held Hawai'i to 13 points and UTEP to seven in its previous two games. San José State needs to sustain drives against that group, and its past two games haven't given me much confidence it can. QB Nathan Hayes is coming off a career-high four touchdown passes, but the Bison finished Saturday by adding defensive tackles as blockers and handing the ball to DJ Scott to run out the clock. With North Dakota State favored here, I expect it to lean on the running game if it gets ahead. I'll back its defense to keep San José State from turning this into a game Hayes has to win through the air. Bet: Under 39.5 (+100)

picks.headline: Staff Picks: Will No. 17 Oklahoma Finish the Regular Season With a Win at No. 23 Missouri?
picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Will No. 17 Oklahoma Finish the Regular Season With a Win at No. 23 Missouri? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games NBA Cup: Knockouts set Friday's college football scores Steelers dominate without Rodgers Luka shoved by fan USWNT qualifies for 2027 World Cup Oklahoma Sooners defensive back Jeremiah Newcombe (21) celebrates after a sack against Texas A&M. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Ryan Chapman · Oklahoma Sooners On SI Fri, November 27, 2026 at 1:46 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads With seven straight November wins in their pocket dating back to last year, the Sooners have a chance to finish the season with nine wins. Not too bad, considering they were just 4-4 and limping to the finish line less than a month ago. Can interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten sustain enough of those quarter-eating, length-of-the-field possessions at Faurot Field to push the Sooners to their fourth straight victory and an 8-4 regular -season finish - and a 6-3 mark in Southeastern Conference play? The Tigers lost three of four games (to No. 9 Ole Miss, No. 7 Texas and No. 1 Georgia) before bouncing back with a big win over Kentucky in Columbia last week. Their defense isn't good, but their offense will score. Can the Sooners keep up? Final Score: Missouri 28, Oklahoma 27 Missouri represents another step up for Jason Witten and the OU offense to deal with. The Tiger defense is comparable, though different, than Texas A&M's unit, but the offense can actually put points on the board and assert pressure if the Sooners come up empty on possessions. Oklahoma's defense needs to have a good tackling day to get Missouri's offense behind the chains. That could help OU force turnovers, which the Tigers have not often given out throughout the year. Missouri can also rush the passer, which will be a big test for John Mateer's decision making. If he can get the ball out quickly, the Sooners will have a chance to make the plays on both sides of the ball to win a tight one. Final Score: Oklahoma 17, Missouri 16 Oklahoma looks like a totally different team than it did earlier in the year. The Sooners' defense is still one of the nation's best. And while the offense isn't a high-flying attack, it has improved significantly. The Sooners have averaged 25 points per game since they parted ways with Ben Arbuckle and promoted Jason Witten to be the interim offensive coordinator. OU's complementary brand of football has allowed the Sooners to climb to No. 17 in the College Football Playoff rankings - just a few weeks after the season seemed lost in late October. The Sooners will cap off their turnaround with an impressive road win against Missouri. Final Score: Oklahoma 31, Missouri 23 This matchup is extremely intriguing. Oklahoma's defense hasn't been tested in a major way over the last two games for various reasons - the weather vs. Ole Miss made it almost impossible for Trinidad Chambliss to push the ball through the air; and Texas A&M's offense was inept. But Missouri is a different animal. Jamal Roberts is probably the best running back the Sooners have faced this season; Austin Simmons has 25 touchdowns with just four interceptions through the air and the Tigers have one of the best receiver duos around in Cayden Lee and Donovan Olugbode. The secondary in particular will be tested in a way they haven't been since at least Texas. Oklahoma will need do tackle well defensively, make enough disruptive plays to keep Simmons out of rhythm, establish the run offensively and at least get enough explosive plays to keep the Tigers' defense honest. If they're able to do that, the Sooners have a good chance of escaping Columbia with their first win there since 2006. Final Score: Oklahoma 20, Missouri 17 Brady Trantham Jason Witten's offense has improved each week in terms of being able to perform more tasks and execute with consistency. Not to mention the subtle uptick in scoring with each outing and you have a Sooner offense that is playing with confidence for the first time in 2026. OU's balanced attack, with John Mateer's legs now a big part of the equation, proves too much for the Tigers' stout but leaky defense. Sooners force a few turnovers to make Missouri's final home game of the year a nightmare. away.blurb: Oklahoma vs. Texas A&M injury report: Who's out and who has to step up for the Sooners Skip to main content Recruiting OL Ryan Fodje: GAME-TIME DECISION Fodje injured his ankle in the loss to Kentucky and has been sidelined ever since. He was ruled out early in weeks until last week, when he was listed as doubtful before ultimately being unavailable against Ole Miss. He was questionable on Friday's report before becoming a game-time decision. Replacement: Although he's the starter at RG on the depth chart, Fodje could also replace E'Marion Harris at right tackle when he returns to the lineup. In the meantime, Heath Ozaeta has been anchoring that RG spot while Fodje has been out. Cornerback Dakoda Fields, who transferred from Oregon this offseason, has been out the last three games, and now, it's four after being listed as questionable until right before kickoff. RB Tory Blaylock: GAME-TIME DECISION Running back Tory Blaylock was also a game-time decision a week (and a day) ago before carrying the ball nine times for 48 yards, averaging 5.3 yards per carry. He's been a regular on the availability report after being banged up since before the season even kicked off, but he has still missed only the opener. He was listed as probable most of this week. Replacement: Freshman Jonathan Hatton Jr. will get touches whether Blaylock is available or not, but he should get even more if Blaylock is on the sidelines. We also had a brief Xavier Robinson sighting last week, so no Blaylock could help Robinson get on the field more. CB Dezz Ricks: game-time decision Everything seems to be going right for the Oklahoma Sooners right now, including a shrinking injury report. The No. 22 Sooners host Texas A&M on Saturday in Norman for a reunion between two old Big 12 rivals. OU, at 6-4, is eyeing a three-game winning streak and just appeared in the CFP rankings for the first time this season after back-to-back ranked wins. A lot of that newfound success is because of a change at offensive coordinator, with tight ends coach Jason Witten replacing Ben Arbuckle, but there's no doubt the Sooners getting healthier is also a major factor. It's not a long list, but there are still a few player statuses to keep an eye on before kickoff. This is the closest we've been in five weeks to seeing Ryan Fodje on the football field. If Fodje returns today, it would be the first time this season the Sooners have their full starting offensive line healthy. Before his injury, Fodje had started every game but the season opener, during which he was also injured. He's listed as the starter at right guard, but he hasn't actually played there yet this season. He filled in for Michael Fausi at left tackle for the five games he was healthy. The Huskies picked a terrific time to play their best ball of the year, including wins at Purdue, Nebraska, and Michigan State before all but ruining Indiana's season last week in a 27-24 overtime thriller. Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Washington vs Oregon: Quick Hits Washington has won two straight and four of its last five games. Oregon is trying to close out its fourth straight regular season with at least a five-game winning streak. Oregon has won both games against Washington since the two programs joined the Big Ten. Washington's two wins over Oregon in 2023 won it the Pac-12 Championship on the way to playing for the national title. How To Watch Washington vs Oregon Date: Saturday, November 28, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: NBC Location: Autzen Stadium, Eugene, OR – Week 13 Schedule, Game Previews – CFP and Bowl Projections Why Washington Will Win The Huskies have been solid all year against the run, and there have only been a few meltdowns, but even when there's a little bending, there's not a lot of breaking. But the story has been the Dawgs trying to run the ball a bit more, and it meant everything against Indiana. This is hardly Army when it comes to the ground game, but quarterback Demond Williams Jr. took over against the Hoosiers, the offense made a point to grind it out a bit, and it set the tone early on against one of the nation's best run defenses. Yes, Oregon is playing well lately, but Michigan ran for 215 yards against the Duck D, Ohio State gave up on the ground and started winging it, and Michigan State was too battered to do anything right. Stay physical, and the Huskies can take control right away. Why Oregon Will Win Oregon is finally playing like a team that knows it's really good. The talent was there from the start of the season, but the Ducks were stunningly sleepy. Quarterback Dylan Raiola has settled in, and now he's playing with confidence. The throws are more decisive, the running game is sharper, and the turnovers that were a disaster in the loss to UCLA, and an issue in the middle of the season have slowed. The Ducks haven't turned it over in any of the last three games, and penalties aren't an issue. Basically, the team is playing better and sharper, and Washington usually needs takeaways. It didn't come up with any in the win over Indiana, but before that, the team was 5-0 when forcing multiple takeaways, and 1-4 when it didn't. Everyone is putting it in the College Football Playoff, which not only assumes a win in the Big Ten Championship, but also a win over Washington to get there first. Can the Huskies be salty like they were against Indiana? Yes, and they're going to make it a much nastier fight than the coronation the Ducks might like. It'll be close throughout, but the Oregon pass rush will start taking over late in a terrific primetime battle (even if it's at the same time as Auburn vs Alabama). No. 12 Oregon is likely in the Big Ten championship game with a win, placing itself firmly in the College Football Playoff picture. No. 24 Washington, meanwhile, would love nothing more than to play spoiler for Dan Lanning’s team and capitalize on momentum picked up in its upset win over Indiana. Here is a preview of Saturday’s contest: No. 12 Oregon (8-3, 6-2 Big Ten) vs. No. 24 Washington (7-4, 4-4) When: Saturday, Nov. 28 Time: 4:30 p.m. PT Where: Autzen Stadium Latest line: Oregon by 13.5 points TV: NBC/Peacock Radio: Oregon Sports Network RUNNING BACK DEPTH Oregon’s top two running backs, Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill Jr., are both listed as questionable for Saturday’s contest. Davison has missed three straight games with a lower leg issue, while Hill got banged up in the first quarter of last Friday’s 45-7 win over Michigan State. While Hill left the field not putting any weight on his left leg, Lanning said postgame that he doesn’t expect the injury to be long-term. Still, his status remains up in the air even as Davison progresses toward a return. The Ducks should be fine either way, though, with the emergence of freshman Brandon Smith as a physical and elusive presence out of the backfield. NEARING A RECORD Matayo Uiagalelei is two sacks away from breaking the Oregon career mark of 29.5 set by Nick Reed. This Washington team gives up a lot of pressure and hits to the quarterback, setting up a favorable situation for Uiagalelei to place his name in the history books on senior day. This could be Uiagalelei’s final game at Autzen Stadium, barring a first-round College Football Playoff game hosted in Eugene. That adds to the motivation for him to get after Demond Williams with regularity. KEEPING CONTAIN Speaking of Williams, the Ducks’ dominant defense will face one of its biggest tests of the season in the elusive signal-caller. Williams’ ability to scramble will be something Oregon’s linebackers will need to monitor all night, and he should have a full complement of pass-catching weapons as well. While you were going for a second helping of stuffing or digging into the pumpkin pie on Thursday, Washington wideouts Dezmen Roebuck and Chris Lawson were upgraded from questionable to probable. Given the Huskies’ issues consistently running the ball, those two will be prominently featured in their upset attempt.
