around after a bad start, and the Washington Huskies are having a good season as well, but the Ducks need this win to improve their College Football Playoff chances. The Oregon Ducks have only a 63% chance of making the College Football Playoff, according to A to Z Sports' CFP Simulator and Predictor . With a win over Washington, that improves to 78%. So, what are the experts saying about this game? Final Score Predictions for Oregon vs. Washington Oregon 24, Washington 18: Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame I expect this to be a physical, defensive-minded rivalry game where Washington makes Oregon work for everything early. Dylan Raiola could have a difficult start, with the Huskies doing a good job of making things uncomfortable and forcing him to settle into the game. However, I think Raiola will find his footing as the afternoon progresses. Oregon has too much offensive talent to stay quiet for four quarters, and I expect the Ducks to make the necessary adjustments to start moving the football more consistently. Washington will remain competitive, but Oregon’s ability to make plays in key situations will ultimately be the difference. The biggest difference in this matchup will be Oregon’s ground game, specifically running back Dierre Hill. I expect Hill to have a major impact, providing the Ducks with some much-needed offensive consistency while taking pressure off Raiola. His ability to create explosive plays and keep the offense ahead of the chains will be critical down the stretch. Washington will make this interesting into the fourth quarter, but Oregon’s balance offensively and ability to control the game on the ground will be enough to get it done. Oregon survives a tough rivalry test, taking down Washington 24-18. Oregon 37, Washington 20: Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama This game suddenly has massive implications as the Oregon Ducks can make up ground in their chase for a College Football Playoff spot. But the game won't be easy. If you saw what happened last week between Washington and Indiana, the Huskies are out to play spoiler. The truth, however, is that the Ducks have been much better since making a change at OC, and quarterback Dylan Raiola has looked very comfortable. Washington let a bad Indiana team run up the score on them, and it almost cost them. This week, it will. Give me the ducks in a big one. Oregon 34, Washington 31: Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida Well, this game certainly got interesting over the last few weeks! It's already one of the nation's underrated rivalries, but after massive wins by both programs over Ohio State and Indiana, respectively, they are both riding high going into this matchup, and the Ducks somehow have a shot at making the College Football Playoff. This game could be the best one of the weekend, with Dylan Raiola and Demond Williams playing their best football of the season, and I think the Ducks get the last laugh. Oregon 34, Washington 23: Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee The Ducks come into this contest riding a wave of momentum, having won four in a row including a statement 41-28 win over Ohio State in Columbus. The Huskies just made their own statement with a 27-24 overtime win over Indiana that put the Hoosiers between a rock and a hard place when it comes to the playoff rankings. Can the Huskies shake up the Big Ten for a second week in a row? Not in Autzen Stadium and not against this Ducks team. The Huskies have been playing competitive football lately, and I think that trend continues. But the big plays they gave up last week to Charlie Becker (six grabs for 167 yards and a 74-yard touchdown) are a sign of more big plays on Saturday by Dylan Raiola and his receivers. This one stays close on the scoreboard, but the Ducks remain in control throughout to do their part to earn a trip to the Big Ten Championship Game. When: 9:15 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 21 Where: Mountain America Stadium in Tempe, Arizona Radio: 96.1 KXXY and The Varsity Sports Network Oklahoma State Record: 6-4 (4-3 Big 12) Arizona State Record: 6-4 (4-3 Big 12) >> Watch Crashing the Boards Below: Loss to Texas Tech was a reality check for Oklahoma State Oklahoma State can put up points with any team in the nation. Oklahoma State has scored 30 points in eight games this season, marking the first time it's accomplished that feat since 2018. With two games left on the regular-season schedule, the Cowboys could tie for sixth-most 30-point games in a season in program history. The 2018 and 2016 teams also scored at least 30 points 10 times. Including the bowl game, Oklahoma State has a chance at 11 30-point games this season. That would tie for the third most in a season with the 2017, 2012, and 1988 teams. The Cowboys are 3-0 in games following a loss this season. Oklahoma State lost to Texas Tech at home last weekend, and it aims to bounce back against an Arizona State squad with the same record overall and in Big 12 play. If the Cowboys win this weekend, the 2026 season would mark the program's first in which Oklahoma State has won each of its first four games immediately following a loss. In the three victories following losses this season, the Cowboys have scored 39 points (vs. Oregon), 57 points (vs. Colorado), and 66 points (vs. Kansas State). >> Video Below: Oklahoma State Cowboys prepare for road game against Arizona State This game marks the seventh overall meeting between Oklahoma State and Arizona State. Four of those meetings have occurred in the past five years. The series is split at 3-3, and the Cowboys hold a 2-1 advantage in games played at Arizona State. Oklahoma State also has won two of the last three matchups. Eric Morris has never faced Arizona State as a head coach, and Sun Devils head coach Kenny Dillingham is 1-1 against Oklahoma State.
